papers.abstract: This article presents a comprehensive review of technologies, tools, and applications in the field of brain-computer interfaces (BCI) and artificial intelligence (AI) for developing cognitively adaptive learning environments. Unlike prior reviews that treat BCI hardware, AI decoding models, and pedagogical deployment as separate topics, this review develops an integrated cross-layer taxonomy linking hardware constraints, AI architecture requirements, and classroom deployment conditions. Emphasis is placed on the transition from cumbersome laboratory systems to wearable hybrid solutions combining electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), as well as textile sensors that offer a favorable trade-off between neurophysiological signal quality and mobility in real-world classroom settings. The review includes a detailed analysis of modern AI architectures, transformer-based models for processing non-stationary neural signals, and Siamese neural networks implementing a few-shot learning paradigm to address the calibration problem associated with new users. It further proposes a unified state-estimation framework integrating cognitive load, attention, and affect into a single formalization for closed-loop adaptive learning systems. The review concludes with a critical analysis of fundamental barriers to scalability, signal instability, mental state privacy issues, and the risk of a neurocognitive divide arising from unequal access to technology. The authors argue that the future of neuroeducation lies in the symbiotic interaction of humans and AI, supported by unified international standards and the convergence of BCI with large language models (LLM) for predictive communication.

papers.title: A Bioinformatics Data Platform on Snowflake Using Life-Science Ontologies as Context for AI Agents
papers.authors: Koreeda T, Kurogi N, Yagi R.
papers.abstract: Life-science ontologies describe concepts such as genes, phenotypes, diseases, and chemical entities under shared identifiers and hierarchies, and over a quarter of a century they have become a foundation for annotation and analysis in bioinformatics. AI agents now assemble research procedures on their own, choosing and running databases and analysis tools, and how well they work depends on the definitions of meaning they can consult, that is, on the context layer. In enterprise data platforms, this layer is increasingly built as an organization-internal operational ontology, as exemplified by Palantir, whereas reference ontologies in the life sciences are maintained by communities outside any single organization. Using Snowflake as an example, we discuss an architecture composed of semantic views that define the meaning of internal data, Cortex Agent that queries through them, and custom tools and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that reach external ontologies. The results of concept resolution and mapping obtained from outside are stored by a custom tool in tables within Snowflake for each query, and are joined with internal data under the semantic view and under the same access control. Taking target–disease matching in drug discovery and cohort definition in real-world data as hypothetical use cases, we show, as a conceptual design, that the set of entities to be matched changes with how far the ontology hierarchy is traversed, and that the temporal conditions of a cohort are applied to the same records as the concept set obtained from the ontology.

papers.title: Vascular dementia and vascular cognitive impairment-current treatments and future prospects.
papers.authors: Markus HS.
papers.journal: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society
papers.abstract: Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) and vascular dementia (VaD) represent a substantial and growing global health burden, yet remain under-recognized and comparatively under-researched. Two broad categories are post-stroke cognitive impairment, and VCI secondary to chronic cerebrovascular disease of which the most common cause is cerebral small vessel disease (SVD). In addition, cerebrovascular pathology frequently coexists with Alzheimer's disease (AD), increasing the probability that AD pathology will manifest as clinical dementia. Current management focuses primarily on prevention through modification of cardiovascular risk factors and lifestyle interventions. Intensive blood-pressure control has shown the strongest evidence, reducing future all-cause dementia while slowing progression of white-matter abnormalities. Multidomain lifestyle interventions incorporating exercise, diet, cognitive training, and vascular risk monitoring may also preserve cognition, although results across trials remain variable. In established VCI and VaD, treatment options are limited; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine lack convincing evidence of benefit, and no pharmacological therapy has definitively demonstrated symptomatic improvement or delayed disease progression. Advances in understanding SVD and VCI pathophysiology are, however, identifying promising therapeutic targets. Emerging evidence highlights endothelial dysfunction, impaired cerebral autoregulation, increased blood-brain barrier permeability, inflammation, and glymphatic dysfunction as possible mechanisms underlying SVD. Current trials are evaluating treatment approaches based on this framework including cerebral vasodilators such as cilostazol, isosorbide mononitrate and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors, anti-inflammatory therapies, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, remote ischemic conditioning, and strategies targeting glymphatic function. Improved mechanistic understanding, appropriately targeted interventions, and adequately powered long-term clinical trials are required to translate these emerging approaches into effective treatments for VCI and VaD.

papers.title: What Does a Donor Need to Know? Content Analysis of Informed Consent Documents Used for Brain Organoid Research.
papers.authors: Hale ZJ, Beretta A, Cohn B, MacDuffie KE.
papers.abstract: Donors of cells used to create induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and brain organoids may not understand what brain organoids are, how they will be used, or the long-term implications of the research. Informed consent documents (ICDs) often contain highly technical language and are written at reading grade levels higher than those attained by the target population. Our goal was to evaluate informed consent documents used for brain organoid research. We compared 20 currently active, IRB-approved consent documents to published templates/guidelines for iPSC research consent. Analyzed ICDs adhered to guidelines in explaining risks and benefits, de-identification, commercial potential, storage, and results sharing. However, descriptions of current and future use were lacking in detail, and the average reading level of ICDs far exceeded that of the general population. Our findings suggest additional transparency in ICDs would assist participants in making an informed choice about participation in iPSC and brain organoid research.

papers.title: Bridging the Gap Between Design and Access: Toward Visual Scene Displays for Brain-Computer Interface Use in Augmentative and Alternative Communication by Children.
papers.authors: Pitt KM, Sawall J, Butler E, Bubak A, Behboodi A.
papers.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
papers.abstract: Purpose Brain-computer interface (BCI) may support communication and computer interaction through neural signals such as the P300 event-related potential (ERP). As a step toward integrating photographic visual scene displays (VSDs) in BCI, this study examined the feasibility of incorporating contextual, naturalistic scenes in which communication items were embedded asymmetrically. Method To evaluate the effects of contextual scene use, 24 neurotypical children aged 8-13 years completed three experimental conditions: (1) a contextual scene with asymmetrical item placement, (2) an asymmetrical arrangement of the same items without contextual information, and (3) a standard grid. Electroencephalogram data were analyzed for the N170, P300, and N400 ERP components, and offline (predicted) BCI augmentative and alternative communication accuracy was calculated. Results The results showed that asymmetry increased frontal and centro-parietal P300 amplitudes, and the scene enhanced occipital N170. Offline BCI performance was similar across the scene and grid conditions, and participants rated the scene as more visually appealing. Conclusion These findings indicate that asymmetry and contextual embedding within scenes may enhance neural engagement and user experience, providing a preliminary foundation for considering photographic VSDs into pediatric BCI research.

papers.title: Sentence Completion Expressive Language Task-Preschool: Preliminary Evidence of Validity and Feasibility for the Neuroimaging Environment.
papers.authors: Washington KN, Kokotek LE, Altaye M, Vannest J, DiFrancesco M, Maloney T.
papers.journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
papers.abstract: Purpose This preliminary investigation occurred across two studies and examined validity, discriminant accuracy, and feasibility of the Sentence Completion Expressive Language Task-Preschool (SCELT-P) for characterizing language production in a neuroimaging environment for typically developing (TD) preschoolers and those with developmental language disorder (DLD). Method Two separate studies were completed. Study 1 (validity) included 82 preschoolers (50% female; 69 TD, 13 DLD) aged 4;0 (years;months) to 5;11 (M age = 4;7). All children were assessed using standardized language measures (e.g., Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-Second Edition), a play-based language sample (analyzed using Developmental Sentence Scoring), and the 30-item SCELT-P (outside the neuroimaging environment), later streamlined to 20 items (SCELT-P Revised [SCELT-PR]). Study 2 (feasibility) included 14 preschoolers (M age = 4;9, 43% female; nine TD, five with DLD) that were assessed using the SCELT-P (inside the neuroimaging environment) and functional magnetic resonance imaging using a sparse acquisition approach with a "listen" (passive) and "listen + speak" (active) condition implemented using DirectRT software. Results In Study 1, the SCELT-P and SCELT-PR demonstrated high reliability, including interrater (intraclass correlation coefficient = .99), test-retest (r = .86 and .80, respectively), and internal consistency (Cronbach's α > .86 and .83, respectively), and similar strong criterion validity (r = . 53-.84). Area under the curve analyses (.91) revealed both versions also evidenced fair sensitivity (.88 and .87) and specificity (.85) rates with a cutoff score of 15.5 and 9.5, respectively. In Study 2, 89% of TD preschoolers and 60% of preschoolers with DLD successfully completed the SCELT-P/R inside the neuroimaging environment, with activation maps illustrating relatively similar neurobiological characteristics across preschoolers in some brain regions. Conclusion The SCELT-P, including its streamlined version, the SCELT-PR, holds promise as a reliable and valid task for including 4- to 5-year-olds in the neuroimaging environment to inform neural and cognitive systems involved in language development. Supplemental material https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34543209.

papers.title: An amygdala-mediated simulation-to-decision cascade aligns interbrain dynamics to solve social dilemmas.
papers.authors: Ni J, Meng F, Zhang C, Tan H, Zeng X, Yang J, Li H, Qi Y, Yan Y, Zhang Y, Zhang K, Ma Y.
papers.abstract: Mutual cooperation (MC) requires independent decision-makers to coordinate under uncertainty about each other's intentions. Using simultaneous intracranial electroencephalography from epilepsy-patient dyads playing a real-time iterated prisoner's dilemma, we identified neurocognitive mechanisms that enable interacting brains to align during mutual cooperation. Amygdala interbrain representational alignment (IBRA), similarity in fine-grained neural spectral patterns across partners, emerged selectively during MC and predicted trial-by-trial outcomes. Early θ-suppression-characterized IBRA reflected rapid, history-sensitive alignment, whereas later IBRA, characterized by low-frequency suppression and γ increases, supported coordinated commitment and action. Furthermore, mutual cooperation relied on an amygdala-mediated, simulation-to-decision cascade, operationalized here as a model-based prospective estimate of partner cooperation that guided self-choice. Amygdala low-frequency suppression tracked this prospective estimate of partner cooperation and θ-γ coupling linked this partner estimate to self-decision processes. Conditional cooperators strategically relied on partner tracking, whereas unconditional cooperators leveraged dispositional tolerance of uncertainty to transition into anticipatory neural alignment. These findings reveal the neural interdependency underpinning MC, redefining cooperation not as isolated decision-making but as a dynamic, interbrain, cognitive alignment.

papers.title: Cortex-wide imaging in naturally behaving mice with 1-gram wireless mesoscopes.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Li A, Yuan L, Wang M, Zhao W, Wang Z, Zang B, Zhou Y, Yu T, Gao L, Wu Y, Zhu R, Tian M, Li K, Wu J, Dai P, Dai Q.
papers.abstract: Revealing how distributed cortical circuits coordinate behavior in freely moving animals remains a central challenge in systems neuroscience, constrained by limited fields of view, low throughput, and the tethering required by current miniaturized microscopes1-4 . Here, we present Airscope, a wireless mesoscope delivering 4 μm lateral resolution across a 6 mm field of view at 12.5 Hz, weighing 1.0 gram. An aspheric-lens design achieves a 2.84× shorter total track length than previous miniaturized microscopes1,2,5,6 while matching the neuron yield of benchtop one-photon mesoscopes; a tailored wireless link supports cable-free calcium imaging from >8,500 neurons per animal (25‑fold increase). Paired with a zero-shot behavior analyzer, Airscope enables cortical imaging across rich behavioral conditions, including room-scale enriched arenas, swimming assays, and multi-organ implantation, with concurrent recording from multiple animals. Using Airscope, we demonstrate versatile applications of untethered cortical imaging across diverse behavioral paradigms. We identify cortical activity patterns across multiple dorsal regions that correlate with behavioral signatures of social dominance, and show dorsal-cortical population activity prospectively decodes competition outcomes across paired animals. We observe reward-location-associated cortical activity patterns during maze exploration, and characterize Granger-causal influence from spinal cord to cortex during fear conditioning, enabled by simultaneous brain-spinal recordings. By uniting large-scale, cellular-resolution recording with unconstrained behavior, Airscope makes naturalistic, multi-animal cortical recording experimentally practical, and provides a broadly accessible technology for systems neuroscience.

papers.title: Predicting trail-making test performance using 7-Tesla structural cerebral MRI.
papers.authors: Schnellbächer GJ, Rajkumar R, Veselinović T, Ramkiran S, Hagen J, Collee M, Shah NJ, Neuner I, Dammers J.
papers.abstract: Psychopharmaceutical therapy has seen a lack of improvement in efficacy, highlighting the need for a more individualized treatment approach that optimally leverages pharmaceutical effects. To achieve this, it is necessary to identify factors that can predict psychological attributes and treatment outcomes. We hypothesize that brain morphology may serve as a predictor of performance in psychological tests. A 7-Tesla-MRI system was used to measure 74 transdiagnostic patients and 41 healthy controls. Values for grey matter volume (GMV), cortical thickness and gyrification based on the Schaefer 100 Atlas for parcellation were determined. Using this morphological data, performance in a Trail-Making Test (TMT) - A and B was predicted with the help of a deep learning model. A SHAP analysis was conducted to identify the key variables important for the model. The accuracy in predicting TMT performance was very good at 0.795. The most decisive feature influencing predictions was gyrification. Areas indicating inter-group differences were focused in the frontal cortex, as well as in temporal and parietal regions. Morphological characteristics can predict test performance with high accuracy. These results support the implementation of a transdiagnostic approach in clinical practice to better address the underlying pathophysiology. Symptom prediction based on neuroimaging data appears to be an achievable goal.

papers.title: Neural correlates of self-directed violence: A large-sample resting-state fMRI study from UK Biobank.
papers.authors: Lin JY, Chi IJ, Zhu JD, Yang AC.
papers.abstract: Background Suicide remains a leading cause of death worldwide, underscoring the importance of identifying neurobiological markers associated with suicidal behaviors. While nonsuicidal self-directed violence (NSSDV) is an established risk factor for future suicide attempts (SAs), the underlying neural distinctions between these behaviors remain insufficiently understood. Methods A total of 1,070 participants with a history of self-directed violence (SDV) were stratified into SA (n = 579) and NSSDV (n = 491) groups based on self-reported questionnaires. All data were collected from the UK Biobank between October 2016 and January 2024. Whole-brain connectome across 90 brain regions were analyzed. A general linear regression model was employed to identify significant functional connectivity (FC) correlations with SA. An exploratory analysis examined the correlation between FC and SDV frequency and recency. Results Compared to NSSDV, the SA group exhibited decreased FC in the bilateral amygdala and right putamen, alongside increased FC in the right caudate. Higher frequency of SDV was correlated with increased FC between the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) and occipital regions, whereas individuals reporting SDV within the past 12 months showed trends of decreased FC between the OFC and both the rectus gyrus and temporal lobe. Conclusions This large-sample rs-fMRI study highlights distinct FC alterations associated with different dimensions of self-harm. Results implicated that the limbic and reward circuits appear particularly relevant in differentiating SA from NSSDV and in capturing variations tied to SDV frequency and recency. These insights advance our understanding of suicidal behaviors' neurobiological underpinnings and may inform targeted risk stratification.

papers.title: EEG Resting-State Beta Band Dynamic Functional Connectivity Reveals State-Dependent Disruption of Language Network Lateralisation in First-Episode Schizophrenia.
papers.authors: Aubonnet R, Fiori Nastro F, Di Lorenzo C, Hassan M, Gargiulo P, Seri S, semantico working group, Di Lorenzo G.
papers.abstract: Language disorganisation is a core feature of schizophrenia with significant functional consequences. However, its neurophysiological substrates remain poorly characterised, particularly in the early stages of the illness. This study investigated whether first-episode schizophrenia (FES) is associated with disruption in the organisation of language-network lateralisation, using both static and dynamic functional connectivity metrics in the EEG beta band. Thirty-one FES patients and 32 age-matched healthy volunteer subjects (HVS) underwent resting-state 64-channel EEG. Source-level connectivity was estimated using the weighted phase lag index with sliding windows, yielding 979 connectivity matrices per participant. Brain network states (BNS) were identified via k-means clustering. Static connectivity was obtained by time-averaging. Temporal features, graph-theoretical metrics, and language-network laterality indices were extracted for both whole-network and language-specific analyses. Group comparisons used permutation-based tests with family-wise error correction. Static connectivity yielded no significant group differences in any metric. Dynamic analysis identified six BNS. FES showed a significant increase in the variability of the temporal dynamics and graph-theory features of BNS5, a state characterised by parieto-occipital dominance. The core language network laterality index was significantly reduced in FES within BNS1, a state characterised by auditory-visual dominance. BNS1 occurrence correlated negatively with language disorganisation scores. Dynamic BNS-specific language network metrics correlated with verbal fluency performance exclusively in FES. These findings demonstrate that language dysfunction in early psychosis is expressed as state-dependent disruption of brain network stability and language lateralisation, detectable only through dynamic connectivity analysis.

papers.title: A shape deformation-based framework for constructing individualized subcortical morphological networks.
papers.authors: Lu S, Zhang J, Li J, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Individualized morphological brain networks have emerged as an important framework for imaging-based connectomics. However, existing methods have focused predominantly on the cerebral cortex, leaving subcortical structures largely unexplored despite their central roles in cognition and neuropsychiatric disorders. Here, we developed a novel framework for constructing individualized subcortical morphological networks from structural magnetic resonance imaging. Specifically, subcortical surfaces were reconstructed using a Point2Mesh-optimized multilayer perceptron architecture and vertex-wise shape deformation was quantified as the signed Euclidean distance between each vertex on an individual mesh and the corresponding vertex on the group-average template mesh. Interregional morphological connectivity in local shape deformation distributions was subsequently estimated using Jensen-Shannon Divergence. Applying this approach to the Human Connectome Project dataset, we found that subcortical morphological networks exhibited complex topological organization, including small-world architecture, modular organization, and highly connected hubs, which were consistently preserved at finer subregional scales. Analyses using an independent test-retest dataset further demonstrated fair-to-good reliability of these network properties. Importantly, these shape deformation-based networks showed significant coupling with subcortical functional networks estimated from resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. Leveraging large-scale multisite clinical datasets, we further demonstrated alterations of subcortical morphological networks in schizophrenia and major depressive disorder. Schizophrenia was characterized predominantly by right caudate-centered disruptions in morphological connectivity and nodal centrality, whereas major depressive disorder exhibited alterations only in nodal centrality of the right amygdala. Together, these findings establish a novel and reliable framework for investigating subcortical morphological network organization in the human brain across both healthy and psychiatric populations.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究提出一种基于形状变形的框架，用于从结构磁共振影像构建个体化皮层下形态学网络：先重建皮层下表面，再以顶点到组平均模板的带符号欧氏距离量化局部形状变形，并用Jensen-Shannon散度估计区域间形态连接。在人类连接组计划数据中，该网络呈现小世界、模块化和高连接枢纽等拓扑组织，且在更细分区尺度上保持一致；独立重测数据表明网络属性具有中等至良好信度，并与静息态功能网络显著耦合。利用多站点临床数据，作者报告精神分裂症主要表现为以右侧尾状核为中心的形态连接和节点中心性异常，重性抑郁障碍仅见右侧杏仁核节点中心性改变。这些结果提示该框架可用于研究健康与精神疾病人群的皮层下形态网络组织，但临床发现基于组间比较，尚不能推断因果或治疗意义。

papers.title: Amplitude-Conditioned Brain Dynamics Reveal Widespread Negative Modulation and Targeted Positive Modulation of Functional Networks.
papers.authors: Salehi MR, BashirGonbadi A, Soltanian-Zadeh H.
papers.abstract: Functional connectivity is traditionally characterized through pairwise interactions between brain regions. However, growing evidence suggests that neural communication is also shaped by higher-order interactions in which the activity of a third region modulates the coupling between others. Here, we introduce a whole-brain framework for mapping resting-state nonlinear conditional connectivity from functional MRI. For each cortical region, we quantified how spontaneous amplitude fluctuations modulate the functional connectivity of all other region pairs. This procedure generated a modulation spectrum for every connection, describing connectivity changes across multiple amplitude states of the modulator. From these spectra, we derived four interpretable features capturing modulatory strength, polarity, volatility, and nonlinear complexity. The framework was applied to resting-state data from the Human Connectome Project and evaluated using stationary surrogate models, spatial topography analyses, test-retest reliability assessments, and behavioral prediction. Surrogate analyses demonstrated that the observed modulation spectra could not be explained by static covariance structure or spectral properties alone, indicating genuine state-dependent dynamic interactions. Topographic mapping reveals a profound functional asymmetry: the macroscopic connectome is dominated by widespread negative modulatory influences, with positive modulation restricted to sparse assortative pathways. Furthermore, by evaluating the effect of temporal integration, we show that spatial and temporal aggregation robustly stabilizes these dynamic fluctuations into reliable, individual-specific traits. Finally, employing regularized predictive modeling, we demonstrate that these dynamic modulatory features can provide complementary predictive value beyond conventional static FC, particularly for capturing state-dependent affective traits such as internalizing behavior. Together, this framework unveils a structured, asymmetric, and behaviorally relevant higher-order modulatory architecture.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究提出一个基于静息态功能磁共振的全脑框架，量化每个皮层区域的自发振幅波动如何调节其他区域对之间的功能连接，并从调节谱中提取强度、极性、波动性和非线性复杂度四个特征。研究使用人类连接组计划数据，通过平稳替代模型、空间拓扑分析、重测信度评估和行为预测进行检验；替代分析表明观察到的调节谱不能仅由静态协方差结构或频谱特性解释。拓扑映射显示宏观连接组以广泛的负向调节为主，正向调节仅见于稀疏的同类通路，且时空聚合能将动态波动稳定为可靠的个体特异性特征。正则化预测建模提示这些动态调节特征在传统静态功能连接之外具有补充预测价值，尤其对内化行为等状态依赖性情感特质；但这是预测关联而非因果或治疗证据，结论受静息态数据与建模条件限制。

papers.title: Parietal Structural and Functional Differentiation Associated with Visual Tracking Across Motor Participation Profiles.
papers.authors: Zhang K, Qi M, Jiang L, Yan Q, Wang Y, Bai S, Cao C, Zhang D, Ma S.
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aimed to examine whether structural and resting-state functional measures of parietal subregions differ across predefined motor participation groups with comparable physical activity levels, and whether these neural measures are associated with visual tracking performance. Methods We adopted an a priori motor-cognitive grouping framework and recruited athletes accordingly, using two representative sports as operational exemplars for each profile: (1) externally driven spatial updating and action planning (ESU; basketball and taekwondo), (2) body-environment calibration and rhythmic sensorimotor integration (SCP; skating and running), and 3) internally guided control and sustained attentional precision (IPS; tai chi and shooting). A sedentary control group (CON) with low habitual physical activity was also recruited. In total, 80 college students participated. Physical activity (PA) was assessed using a standardized questionnaire. All participants underwent structural MRI and resting-state fMRI to derive gray matter volume (GMV), fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (fALFF), degree centrality (DC), regional homogeneity (ReHo), and functional connectivity (FC) within parietal subregions (S1, SPL, AG, and SMG). Supplementary SPL-based FC analyses further examined connectivity with regions of the broader visuospatial and sensorimotor network. Visual tracking was assessed using a multiple object tracking (MOT) task across three difficulty levels. Results PA levels were significantly higher in all athlete groups than in sedentary controls, with no differences among athlete groups. Across structural and resting-state functional measures, the most consistent group differences were selectively concentrated in S1 and SPL, whereas effects involving other parietal regions were less consistent across measures. Specifically, the ESU group exhibited the highest bilateral S1 GMV, the SCP group showed the highest bilateral SPL GMV, and the IPS group demonstrated the highest fALFF in both S1 and SPL. The IPS group also showed the highest ReHo in bilateral SPL. FC differed significantly across several parietal connections, with distinct connectivity patterns across the three athlete groups. MOT accuracy differed significantly across groups at all difficulty levels, with the ESU and IPS groups outperforming the SCP and CON groups overall. Across all participants, multiple S1 and SPL metrics showed modest associations with MOT performance (r = 0.20-0.40). Within athlete subgroups, stronger and task-specific associations were observed, particularly in the SCP and IPS groups (r = 0.50-0.80). Conclusions These findings identify distinct structural and functional patterns predominantly involving S1 and SPL across different motor participation profiles, despite comparable overall physical activity levels among the athlete groups. Such parietal differences are accompanied by difficulty-dependent differences in visual tracking performance and heterogeneous brain-behavior associations. Together, the results highlight S1 and SPL as the parietal regions showing the most consistent differentiation across structural and functional measures in association with distinct motor participation profiles and visual tracking performance, and provide a focused empirical basis for future investigations into the sources of this heterogeneity.

papers.title: Multivariate Prediction of White Matter BOLD Activity and Its Relationship to Marginal Connectivity.
papers.authors: Li M, Ding Z, Gore JC.
papers.abstract: Functional MRI studies have traditionally focused on gray matter, whereas white matter BOLD signals have often been treated as weak or artifactual. However, white matter BOLD fluctuations are robustly detectable and contain reproducible functional information, yet most gray-to-white matter analyses rely on only marginal functional connectivity, which cannot separate pairwise coupling from shared variance among distributed cortical systems. Here, we used a multivariate cortical prediction framework to test whether spontaneous white matter BOLD activity can be predicted from distributed cortical gray matter BOLD activity, and how this predictive structure relates to marginal connectivity. Resting-state fMRI data from 81 Human Connectome Project young adult participants were analyzed using a strict white matter mask with no overlap with cortical predictors. For each white matter voxel, time series from 400 cortical parcels were used to predict white matter BOLD signals with nested leave-one-run-out ridge regression. Cortical BOLD activity modestly but reliably predicted white matter BOLD dynamics, demonstrating consistent cross-validated prediction accuracy across a broad spatial extent of the white matter. Ridge β coefficients strongly recapitulated marginal functional connectivity fingerprints, indicating a shared functional backbone, but their first gradients differed reproducibly. The difference between these gradients defined a β-minus-FC G1 divergence axis that remained stable after broadly controlling for anatomical, signal-related, and spatial factors. At the low end of the axis, enriched in callosal and capsular structures, pairwise gray-to-white matter connectivity was relatively strong, but white matter BOLD fluctuations were predicted less well by distributed cortical BOLD activity than that connectivity would suggest. At the high end, enriched in posterior projection and association pathways, pairwise connectivity was relatively weak, but distributed cortical BOLD activity predicted white matter BOLD signals better than expected. These findings identify a reproducible, tract-organized contrast between marginal connectivity and its covariance-adjusted predictive representation.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注白质BOLD自发活动能否由分布式皮层灰质活动预测，以及这种预测结构与边际功能连接的关系。作者分析81名年轻成人静息态fMRI数据，用严格白质掩膜和400个皮层分区的嵌套留一run岭回归，对每个白质体素做多变量预测。结果显示皮层活动对白质BOLD有适度但可靠的交叉验证预测，岭回归系数与边际连接指纹高度重合，但两者的首要梯度存在可重复差异，形成一条在控制解剖、信号和空间因素后仍稳定的分歧轴。该轴低端以胼胝体和内囊结构为主，成对连接较强但预测弱于连接所暗示；高端以后部投射和联合通路为主，成对连接较弱但预测强于预期，提示边际连接与其协方差校正后的预测表征存在按纤维束组织的可重复对比。

papers.title: DA-S<sup>2</sup>RL: Disease-aware shared-specific representation learning for heterogeneous image-EHR Alzheimer's disease diagnosis.
papers.authors: Wang W, Shi Y, Cheng J, Liu Y.
papers.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
papers.abstract: Combining electronic health records (EHR) with medical images is important for improving the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, neuroimages and EHR differ greatly in semantic content and data distribution. Neuroimages mainly reflect brain structure and metabolic abnormalities, while EHR records clinical symptoms and behavioral changes. Directly fusing these heterogeneous modalities may mix shared disease information with modality-specific diagnostic cues, resulting in redundant and ambiguous representations. To address this problem, we propose DA-S2 RL, a disease-aware shared-specific multimodal representation learning framework for AD diagnosis. DA-S2 RL organizes heterogeneous image and EHR features into disease-related shared semantics and modality-specific diagnostic residuals. The core of DA-S2 RL is the shared-specific cross-modal coding (SCC) module. It strengthens cross-modal semantic consistency, suppresses redundant correlations, and enables mutual refinement between shared semantics and diagnostic residuals. Before SCC, image features are integrated into a compact image representation, and EHR features are encoded into the same feature space. Experiments on ADNI and NACC demonstrate that explicitly organizing heterogeneous image-EHR representations into shared disease semantics and modality-specific residuals improves multimodal diagnostic learning under different image-EHR settings.

papers.title: Reduced Somatomotor Cortical Thickness in Women With PTSD After Childhood Sexual Abuse: A Structural Correlate Distinct From Adult Sexual Dysfunction.
papers.authors: Nkrumah RO, Grießer L, Demirakca T, Brosch K, Zehirlioğlu L, Heim C, Sütterlin M, Ende G, Schmahl C.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
papers.abstract: Background Childhood sexual abuse (CSA) is a major risk factor for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and adult sexual dysfunction in women. Although adverse childhood experiences have been linked to altered brain structure, cortical alterations specifically associated with CSA and PTSD in women remain poorly characterized, and their relationship to adult sexual functioning is unknown. Methods Women with CSA and current PTSD (n = 52), women with CSA without current PTSD (n = 32), and control women without CSA or PTSD (n = 48) underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging. Cortical thickness, surface area, and cortical volume were examined using whole brain vertex wise analyses. Sexual functioning was assessed in a subsample (n = 41). Results Women with CSA and current PTSD showed reduced cortical thickness within a left somatomotor cluster relative to controls (cluster wise p = .017). Anatomical characterization localized the cluster to motor and premotor regions involved in bodily self representation and sensorimotor integration. No group differences were observed in cortical surface area or volume. Women with CSA and PTSD also reported lower sexual functioning, particularly in arousal, lubrication, satisfaction and pain. Cortical thickness within the somatomotor cluster was unrelated to sexual functioning and did not mediate the association between CSA severity and sexual dysfunction. Conclusions These findings suggest that somatomotor cortical alterations represent neurobiological correlates of trauma related psychopathology following CSA in women. The absence of associations with adult sexual functioning suggests that structural alterations within the somatomotor cortex may be distinct from mechanisms contributing to sexual dysfunction.

papers.title: Functional connectivity and treatment response in obesity and eating disorders: Current evidence and empirical data.
papers.authors: Miranda-Olivos R, Soriano-Mas C, De la Peña-Arteaga V, Baenas I, Lucas I, Camacho-Barcia L, Sánchez I, Granero R, Gaspar-Perez A, Sánchez-González J, Fernández-Formoso JA, Guerrero-Pérez F, López-Urdiales R, Vilarrasa N, Jiménez-Murcia S, Fernández-Aranda F.
papers.abstract: Alterations in large-scale brain networks have been reported in obesity (OB) and eating disorders (ED), but their relevance to treatment outcomes remains unclear. We reviewed evidence on neurobiological predictors of treatment outcome in ED and OB and present preliminary empirical analyses exploring baseline rsFC differences between individuals with anorexia nervosa (AN), obesity with comorbid ED (OB + ED), and obesity without ED (OB - ED) and healthy controls (HC), and examining whether these connectivity differences are associated with treatment outcome in the clinical groups. A total of 98 women (AN = 27, OB + ED = 25, OB - ED = 21, HC = 25) underwent resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI). rsFC networks were subsequently identified using probabilistic independent component analysis (ICA), and their associations with treatment outcomes were examined within each clinical group. Both OB groups showed reduced rsFC relative to HC within a thalamic-basal ganglia network, specifically in a cluster located in the left inferior occipital cortex encompassing extrastriate visual regions. Baseline connectivity in this occipital cluster showed a positive, although non-significant, association with treatment outcome in the OB - ED group, whereas no significant associations were observed in AN or OB + ED. Given the non-significant nature of this exploratory association, the observed relationship should be considered hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in adequately powered samples. Further work is needed to clarify the role of sensory-integrative networks in treatment response across extreme weight conditions.

papers.title: Cortical Cholinergic Pathway Degeneration Reflects Cognitive Impairment and Dementia in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.authors: Slater NM, Myall DJ, Shoorangiz R, Meissner WG, Kirk IJ, Keenan RJ, Lee RM, Horne KL, MacAskill MR, Le Heron CJ, Pitcher TL, Anderson TJ, Melzer TR, Dalrymple-Alford JC.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
papers.abstract: Background Cognitive impairment is a prevalent and debilitating feature of Parkinson's disease (PD). Increasing evidence from postmortem and in vivo positron emission tomography imaging studies supports cholinergic dysfunction in PD. There is, however, little evidence regarding the influence of the structural integrity of cortical cholinergic pathways that emanate from the nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM). Objectives To investigate the association between cognition and the structural integrity of medial and lateral cortical cholinergic projection pathways in PD. Methods Neuropsychological assessment, T1 imaging, and high angular resolution diffusion imaging (HARDI) were acquired from 108 participants with PD (41 female, mean age 71.3 years) and 41 control participants (22 female, mean age 70.6 years). Streamlines representing three cortical cholinergic pathways (one medial and two lateral) from the NBM were extracted from anatomically constrained tractography. Structural integrity was compared across controls and cognitive subgroups (PD with normal cognition [PD-N], with mild cognitive impairment [PD-MCI], and with dementia [PDD]) and using a continuous global measure of cognition. Results In PD, we found evidence that lower cognitive performance was associated with increased mean diffusivity across all pathways, especially the perisylvian component of the lateral pathway. In those individuals with dementia, increased free water fraction and decreased fractional anisotropy and fiber density and cross-section was detected across all pathways. Conclusions Degeneration of the cortical cholinergic system is associated with cognitive decline in PD. Future work should determine whether pathway degeneration predicts future cognitive decline and dementia. © 2026 The Author(s). Movement Disorders published by Wiley Periodicals LLC on behalf of International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

papers.title: The translational asymmetry of corpus callosotomy: Two literatures that answered different questions.
papers.authors: Cavalcanti VB, de Aguiar PHP.
papers.abstract: Corpus callosotomy is an established palliative operation for drug-resistant epilepsy dominated by drop attacks, and it is performed in three extents: anterior, usually of the anterior two-thirds; total, in one or two stages; and selective posterior, which preserves the genu and rostral body. Meta-analysis finds no difference between them in overall seizure reduction, a difference in drop attack control favoring the posterior approach, and a graded difference in disconnection syndrome, but there has never been a prospective head-to-head comparison, and the optimal extent of section remains undefined. A search of PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection identified 62 experimental studies in which the corpus callosum or another forebrain commissure was sectioned with an epilepsy-related outcome, spanning 1948-2026 across six species and every major seizure model. This literature is neither absent nor recent. What it has almost never done is vary the extent of section: the few studies that varied it took the laterality of kindling transfer or of interictal synchrony as the endpoint, never seizure control and never cognitive cost. No study compares the three extents against a common outcome; none models the selective posterior operation as it is defined clinically; none randomizes between extents; and none combines graded disconnection with time-locked bilateral electrophysiology, diffusion-based verification of the fibers divided, and a behavioral read-out in the same animals. The effect of section is also bidirectional: focal seizures may intensify through loss of transcallosal inhibition, and in the pentylenetetrazol model callosal section paradoxically facilitates convulsions, which limits chemoconvulsant preparations. The asymmetry between the clinical and experimental literatures is therefore one of method rather than of volume or attention: the two answered different questions, and the question the clinical field now asks requires a manipulation the experimental literature has never performed. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Surgeons can treat severe epilepsies by cutting the bundle of fibers that joins the two halves of the brain, but they do not agree on how much of it to cut. We searched three databases and found 62 animal studies of this operation going back to 1948. Almost none of them compared different amounts of cutting, and none looked at the newest version of the operation. Answering the surgeons' question will require a new kind of animal experiment rather than more reading of the old ones.

papers.title: Early neurocognitive outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation.
papers.authors: Cockle E, Malpas CB, Coleman H, McIlroy A, Laing J, Hunn M, Gutman M, Logan S, Robinson GR, Harb C, Meade C, D'Souza W, Halliday A, Bulluss K, Vogrin S, Alpitsis R, O'Brien TJ, Rayner G, Neal A.
papers.abstract: Objective Characterization of early neuropsychological outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RFTHC) is essential to guide patient expectations around return to work, study, and caregiving. The current study aimed to describe the early neurocognitive sequelae of SEEG. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing SEEG were prospectively recruited from two tertiary epilepsy centers in Melbourne, Australia. Patients were administered the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS) via telehealth before and 3 weeks after SEEG (M = 19.69 days, SD = 4.41). Given the telehealth platform, the coding subtest was substituted for the Symbol Digit Modalities Test, and a modified score of global cognitive function was calculated. To evaluate group changes, paired sample t-tests were performed. Reliable change indices were computed to explore individual-level changes. Pearson's correlation coefficients evaluated relationships between change in global cognitive function and SEEG admission variables. SEEG patients were invited to complete a semi-structured interview canvassing the recovery following SEEG. Results Twenty-eight patients completed the neuropsychological examination (M = 37.89 years, SD = 9.72, range = 17-56 years, 54% female). All patients underwent RFTHC with a mean of 11.43 (SD = 6.87, range = 2-28) coagulation sites. At a whole group level, 3-weeks post SEEG there was no evidence for global nor domain-specific cognitive change. Reliable change indices with 90% confidence revealed only 4% (1/28) declined on at least two measures and 10% (3/28) showed psychometric improvement. Pearson's correlational coefficients showed no evidence for association between change in global cognitive function with SEEG factors including admission length, number of spontaneous or stimulated seizures, number of electrodes, or number of RFTHC sites. Subjective reports of language change tended to be accompanied by a decline on the RBANS language index that did not meet reliable change criteria. Most patients reported returning to work around 4 weeks post SEEG. Significance By 3 weeks, gross cognitive functioning tends to be in keeping with pre-SEEG performances for most patients. These findings have direct clinical implications for SEEG neuropsychological counseling. Plain language statement SEEG is increasingly used to guide epilepsy surgery. Despite this, little is known about the cognitive recovery in the weeks following the procedure. We found that for most patients, broad cognitive functioning 3 weeks after SEEG with coagulation was consistent with function before SEEG, with only a small minority showing significant changes. Some people who reported language difficulties also showed a decline on language testing, although this was often small. Of those patients working before SEEG, most returned to work by 4 weeks. These results provide important evidence to guide patient counseling, recovery planning, and management after SEEG.

papers.title: Validation of the diagnosis of Lennox-Gastaut syndrome: Challenges and lessons learned.
papers.authors: Villalba N, Rosenman M, Lam S, Knupp KG, Thio LL, Welch WP, Randle SC, Garcia-Sosa R, Reed L, Dixon-Salazar T, Carroll M, Patel AD.
papers.abstract: Objective Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome (LGS) is a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy characterized by multiple seizure types, cognitive impairment, and distinct electroencephalographic (EEG) findings. However, evolving diagnostic criteria, heterogeneous clinical features, and inconsistent electronic health record (EHR) documentation complicate accurate diagnosis and cohort identification. As part of a Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute-sponsored study developing EHR-based computable phenotypes for LGS, we established a reference standard through retrospective chart review and epileptologist classification. Methods A multicenter retrospective chart review was conducted across seven pediatric epilepsy centers. Stratified sampling using PCORnet data selected patients based on the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision diagnosis code for LGS or other intractable epilepsy diagnoses between 2016 and 2022. Clinical teams abstracted seizure history, EEG findings, developmental status, and treatment history. Two epileptologists independently reviewed each case as classic LGS, pragmatic LGS, or not LGS. Discordant cases underwent adjudication by a senior epileptologist. Cases with incomplete or unclear data underwent repeat abstraction and review. Results Of 997 identified patients, 935 underwent classification after exclusions. Initial epileptologist disagreement occurred in 105 cases (11%, unweighted Cohen kappa = 82%). Following adjudication, 130 cases underwent reabstraction to retrieve additional EEG reports and clinical details. Rereview reclassified 67 cases initially considered "not LGS": 33 classic LGS, 12 pragmatic LGS, and 22 excluded for insufficient data. Key EHR challenges included inconsistent EEG reporting, incomplete seizure type characterization, fragmented documentation of cognitive impairment, unclear age at onset, and variable terminology across institutions and providers. Slow spike-and-wave EEG findings were the most frequently missing diagnostic element. Significance Validating LGS diagnoses using EHR data is complex and resource intensive. Standardized terminology, structured documentation, and rigorous multicenter validation may improve diagnostic accuracy, research cohort identification, computable phenotype development, and longitudinal care for individuals with LGS. Our results highlight important operational lessons for multicenter rare epilepsy studies and underscore the need for improved diagnosis pathways and longitudinal care systems for those with LGS and their families.

papers.title: Symptom-related damage patterns in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Xu Q, Li K, Zhang Q, Li Y, Li J, Liao W, Li J, Chen Y, Yao X, Yang F, Ji X, Lu G, Zhang Z.
papers.abstract: Objective This study was undertaken to elucidate the neuroanatomical and network substrates underlying diverse seizure symptoms in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (mTLE-HS) by applying multivariate support vector regression (SVR) to individualized structural symptom mapping and atrophy network mapping (ANM). Methods We retrospectively enrolled 216 patients with mTLE-HS and 460 healthy controls. Six non-mutually exclusive seizure symptoms were assessed. We performed left-right flipping of all images of right-sided mTLE-HS patients along the midline before processing the data. Individual atrophy gray matter maps were derived using normative modeling. Structural symptom mapping was performed using multivariate SVR lesion-symptom mapping. For each patient, indirect ANM maps were generated using a normative functional connectome and direct ANM maps using the patient's own resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. Correspondence between the two ANM approaches was assessed using individual-level whole-brain spatial correlations of unthresholded maps and group-level Dice coefficients of thresholded maps. Results Individual structural atrophy patterns were spatially heterogeneous, whereas different seizure manifestations were associated with partially distinct structural patterns and more spatially convergent network-level associations. Focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures were associated with thalamic network involvement, gestural/limb automatisms with anterior cingulate-related networks, ictal vocalization symptoms with perisylvian language networks, dysmnesia with hippocampal-posteromedial networks, emotional phenomena with prefrontal-temporal networks, and autonomic phenomena with medial prefrontal and limbic networks. Furthermore, limited spatial correspondence was observed between the results of the direct and indirect atrophy network analyses, suggesting the indirect and direct ANM can be regarded as nonequivalent but potentially complementary approaches. Significance In mTLE-HS, heterogeneous seizure manifestations are associated with distinct patterns of atrophy and distributed functional network involvement. ANM provides a complementary framework for characterizing symptom-related network patterns, and differences between indirect/normative and direct/patient-specific connectome analyses may provide complementary information.

papers.title: Neurobehavioral Profiles and Clinical Consequences of MYT1L-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Insights From the Brain Gene Registry.
papers.authors: Granadillo JL, Kaster L, Lanzotti V, Grewal D, Schreiber A, Abbacchi AM, Gurnett CA, Kroll KL, Baldridge D, Hazlett HC, Dawalt L, Constantino JN, Gupta A, Dougherty JD.
papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
papers.abstract: MYT1L-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder (MYT1L-NDD) is a rare autosomal dominant syndrome characterized by intellectual disability, global developmental delay, autism, and obesity. Despite growing recognition, prospective and systematic clinical phenotyping remains limited. Here, we present an exploratory analysis of data from 25 individuals with MYT1L-NDD enrolled in the Brain Gene Registry (BGR), a national platform integrating genetic, neurobehavioral, and clinical data. Neurobehavioral assessments were conducted using the Rapid Neurobehavioral Assessment Protocol (RNAP), including virtual adaptations of the Shipley, Developmental Profile-4, ASEBA Child Behavior Checklist, and Vineland-3. Diagnostic and medication data were extracted from structured electronic health records (EHR). MYT1L-NDD participants were compared to the broader BGR cohort. MYT1L-NDD participants exhibited pronounced impairments in nonverbal cognition and adaptive functioning, particularly in motor tasks, communication, and daily living skills. Behavioral assessments revealed elevated rates of autism symptoms, ADHD symptoms, behavioral conduct problems, oppositional defiance, and anxiety. EHR diagnosis data were available for 10 MYT1L-NDD participants. It showed frequent diagnoses of developmental delays, speech and language disorders, intellectual disability, gastrointestinal problems, and obesity. Medication data on five participants indicated common prescription of alpha-2 adrenergic agonists and laxatives. This study provides the first prospective, multi-source characterization of MYT1L-NDD. Findings expand our understanding of MYT1L-NDD phenotypes in a quantitative and systematic manner and support the value of registry-based approaches for understanding rare neurodevelopmental disorders. Larger, longitudinal, age-stratified studies are needed to further define MYT1L-NDD natural history and inform clinical care.

papers.title: Sex shapes capillary flows and oxygen extraction in the middle-aged mouse brain
papers.authors: Gutiérrez-Jiménez E, Wied B, Lindhardt TB, Mikkelsen SH, Knopper RW, Skoven CS, Christensen OB, Dashkovskyi V, Mrotek F, Rasmussen PM, Andresen MH, Krmpot A, Khatib ME, Vinogradov S, Sakadžić S, Jensen MF, Pedroza-Pacheco I, Postnov D, Lin L, Just J, Hansen B, Østergaard L.
papers.abstract: Sex differences in brain aging are well documented, but their origin within the cerebrovascular hierarchy remains unclear. Here we show that cortical blood flow is higher in female than male mice at 15 months of age, at a point when an earlier sex difference in pulsatility and resistance indices has already converged, pial vessel diameter shows no difference between sexes, and estrogen levels are similar between sexes. Using an indicator-dilution and intravascular oxygen measurements using two-photon microscopy, we found that capillary transit-time heterogeneity (CTH) scales more steeply with mean transit time in females, consistent with a passively regulated capillary network, and that this is accompanied by reduced oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) without deficit in arterial oxygen delivery. Spatial transcriptomics reveals that sex differences are organized into distinct regional programs, most prominently in white matter, where a male-associated myelin and axonogenesis signature accompanies reduced white matter volume in females. These molecular and structural differences coincide with elevated hippocampal microglial reactivity and an altered spatial search strategy in females, without any detectable differences in circulating markers of stress, blood-brain barrier integrity, or immunity. Together, these findings indicate that sex differences in the aging brain are expressed at the level of capillary flow regulation and regional tissue programs rather than through bulk cerebral blood flow alone, and that elevated blood flow in females can mask, rather than reflect, adequate tissue oxygenation.

papers.title: The ovarian cycle and estradiol modulate cortical network state and auditory entrainment in mice and women
papers.authors: Carreño-Muñoz MI, Chehrazi P, Ciancone Chama A, Knoth I, Fernandes do Nascimento AS, Campbell BF, Csicsvari J, Chattopadhyaya B, Lippé S, Di Cristo G.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The human brain is remarkably dynamic, continuously adapting to internal and external signals across rapid and protracted timescales. While both male and female brains are influenced by sex hormones to drive adaptive behavioural and physiological changes, the ovarian cycle in female mammals represents a conserved naturalistic model to understand how hormones such as estradiol (E2) alter cellular and network states to shape brain function. To understand whether and how the ovarian cycle influences sensory cortical processing, we investigated cortical network activity at rest and upon auditory stimulation across the ovarian cycle in mice and human subjects. We recorded EEG activity in men and women and intracortical local field potentials in male and female mice. Female participants were tested during two phases of their ovarian cycle characterized by low E2 levels (early follicular phase in women; late estrus in mice) and high E2 levels (late follicular phase in women; proestrus in mice). Across species, high endogenous or exogenous estradiol was associated with a steeper aperiodic power spectral slope, indicating decreased excitatory/inhibitory drive and attenuated auditory entrainment following a 40Hz stimulation. At the single-cell level, high E2 selectively increased the baseline and sustained 40-Hz firing of putative fast-spiking interneurons while reducing their temporal coherence during both spontaneous and stimulus-evoked activity, suggesting that E2 enhances inhibitory tone, while disrupting the temporal coordination of inhibitory networks. Altogether, these findings demonstrate that estradiol dynamically modulates cortical network states and auditory responsiveness. This underscores the necessity of investigating hormone-brain coupling as an evolutionarily conserved model essential for yielding translational insights into sex-specific neurobiology.

papers.title: Adolescent prodromal phenotypes of psychiatric disorders: insights from a novel DISC1-perturbed monkey model
papers.authors: Lan Z, Onoe H, Tsukiyama T, Iwatani C, Chen C, Okita K, Ishizuka K, Endo R, Nakai R, Imamura K, Hikishima K, Tsuchiya H, Nakaya M, Fang Y, Kobayashi A, Shinto Y, Yamaguchi R, Matsunaga M, Oe K, Omori K, Ozeki Y, Tomoda T, Miura K, Urayama S, Oishi N, Okada T, Tanaka M, Inoue H, Takahashi J, Sawa A, Isa T.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Neurodevelopmental deficits frequently lead to mild but significant adolescent social and cognitive changes, representing prodromal manifestations of adult-onset psychiatric disorders in a cross-disease manner. Although experimental medicine utilizes animal models to address the mechanisms, rodent brains lack critical structures for human higher brain functions such as the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. To fill this translational gap, we generated monkeys with an impaired DISC1 gene locus, targeting the multifunctional protein essential for neurodevelopment and involved in transdiagnostic mental health risks. Here we analyze the F0 animals by minimizing mosaicism. At ages equivalent to human adolescence, these monkeys exhibited blunted responsiveness to social stimuli and increased internal drives, mirroring altered social behaviors in the prodromal stage in humans. Resting-state functional MRI data indicated disrupted global functional connectivity and reorganization of network topology, marked by a shift in the dominance of brain hubs from prefrontal regions to sensory areas. This primate model provides a unique platform for studying psychiatric disorders, such as schizophrenia, across the developmental trajectory.

papers.title: Modeling Paralinguistic Features for Speech Neuroprostheses: A Systematic Review
papers.authors: Yenikapati MS, Deshpande S, Desai SP, Santine DD, Roghani AK.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in brain-computer interface (BCI) technology have brought speech neuroprostheses closer to restoring naturalistic communication for individuals with severe motor or speech impairments. Although current systems can decode phonemic and lexical information from cortical activity, they often fail to capture paralinguistic dimensions such as intonation, prosody, loudness, and affect that are essential for conveying emotion and intent. This review synthesizes emerging research on modeling and incorporating paralinguistic features into speech neuroprosthetic design. Foundational studies have mapped the cortical organization of speech production, identifying articulatory somatotopy within the sensorimotor cortex and functional subdivisions across planning, phonological, and semantic representations. More recent work has characterized expressive encoding within the ventral precentral and supplementary motor areas, while peripheral and multimodal sensing approaches have demonstrated promising accuracy in decoding emotional states. Collectively, these findings signal a shift toward closed-loop neuroprosthetic systems that integrate affective modulation with linguistic decoding, enabling restoration of speech that is not only intelligible but expressively human.

papers.title: 5-Aminolevulinic Acid-Guided Glioma Resection During Awake Craniotomy: Systematic Review of Functional Safety and Oncologic Benefit
papers.authors: Mofatteh M.
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Maximal safe resection remains the cornerstone of glioma surgery, particularly in eloquent regions where oncologic gain must be balanced against functional preservation. While 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) fluorescence-guided surgery improves extent of resection in high-grade gliomas under general anesthesia, its role during awake craniotomy (AC) remains underdeveloped. We aimed to evaluate the oncologic and functional outcomes of 5-ALA-guided tumor resection during AC. Methods PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to February 2026 for studies reporting original data on AC using 5‑ALA following PRISMA guidelines. Study quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Results Across 10 studies comprising 108 patients, fluorescence positivity was 76.5% in high‑grade gliomas and 17.5% in low‑grade gliomas. Gross‑total resection was achieved in 57.4% overall, reaching 66.7% in the largest cohort. Transient aphasia occurred in 25.9% of patients, while permanent aphasia and persistent hemiparesis were observed in 8.3% and 14.8%, respectively. In multiple studies, resection was intentionally halted despite persistent fluorescence when functional mapping identified an eloquent cortex, underscoring that mapping remained the decisive determinant of surgical boundaries. No study reported conversion to general anesthesia. Conclusions 5‑ALA-guided resection during AC appears feasible, functionally safe, and clinically useful, particularly for high-grade gliomas in eloquent regions. Across the available literature, 5-ALA consistently enhances intraoperative tumor visualization, supports identification of residual fluorescent disease, and integrates well with cortical and subcortical mapping without clear evidence of increased permanent neurological morbidity. Although functional mapping remains the decisive determinant of the final resection boundary, the available evidence supports 5-ALA as a valuable complementary adjunct in onco-functional glioma surgery. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized volumetric and survival endpoints are now needed to refine patient selection and quantify its added benefit.

papers.title: Long-term memory and microstructural changes after chemotherapy and low-dose radiotherapy covering the whole ventricle in patients with germinoma
papers.authors: Kanamori M, Mugikura S, Mori N, Iizuka O, Shimoda Y, Osada Y, Yamashita S, Shibahara I, Umezawa R, Saito R, Sonoda Y, Kumabe T, Jingu K, Suzuki K, Endo H.
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study assessed memory impairment and underlying microstructural changes in patients with germinoma treated long-term with 24 Gy radiation, which covered the whole ventricle, with chemotherapy (low-dose WVI with chemotherapy). Methods This prospective observational study included patients treated with low-dose WVI with chemotherapy at our departments from 1999 to 2021. Their intelligence and memory were assessed using the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale, 3rd Edition, and the Wechsler Memory Scale, Revised Edition (WMS-R). Diffusion tensor images (DTI) and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) metrics were calculated in white and gray matter and compared to the mean values from 11 age-matched healthy individuals. Associations between DTI and NODDI metrics and WMS-R memory scores were also examined. Results Among 68 patients treated with low-dose WVI with chemotherapy, 32 provided consent for evaluation. The median ages at treatment and evaluation were 17.1 and 24.9 years, respectively. Sixteen (50%) patients had WMS-R index scores below 85 (− 1 standard deviation). Memory was more severely impaired than intelligence or attention. DTI and NODDI metrics showed alterations in extensive gray and white matter regions associated with memory. DTI and NODDI metrics in the fornix, cingulum, cingulate cortex, orbital cortex, and thalamus correlated with memory scores. Conclusion Memory impairment is common in these patients, with microstructural changes in extensive memory-related regions associated with impaired memory function.

papers.title: Epilepsy as an Initial Presentation of Superficial Siderosis of the Central Nervous System:A Case Report
papers.authors: Ma R, Sun J, Luo W, Zhang G, Ren H.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Superficial siderosis of the central nervous system (SSCNS) is a rare neurological disorder resulting from chronic subarachnoid haemorrhage. Its classical clinical features comprise sensorineural hearing loss, cerebellar ataxia and pyramidal tract dysfunction. However, epilepsy as an initial presentation remains uncommon and insufficiently characterized. Case Presentation: We describe a 34-year-old male with a remote history of right brachial plexus injury, who presented with recurrent epileptic seizures as the predominant early symptom, followed by progressive hearing loss and gait instability. Neuroimaging demonstrated characteristic haemosiderin deposition on T2*-weighted and susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) sequences.Transient, seizure-related subcortical and periventricular restricted diffusion on diffusion-weighted imaging resolved completely within one month. Anti-epileptic medication achieved partial seizure control, but the patient’s neurological deficits exhibited gradual progression. Conclusion Epilepsy may represent an uncommon initial presentation of SSCNS. Targeted MRI sequences facilitate diagnosis. SSCNS should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients with unexplained epilepsy,particularly those with a history of craniospinal trauma.

papers.title: Behavioral and neural modulation effects of transcranial pulse stimulation of the dorsal cingulate cortex and anterior insula cortex in healthy adults: A prospective, randomized, sham-controlled trial
papers.authors: Qin PP, Chak IK, Lin TTZ, Jin M, Kan RL, Zhang BB, Xia AW, Wang SX, Lam V, Lin J, Yuan T, Chau BK, Bergmann TO, Padberg F, Kranz GS.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Transcranial pulse stimulation (TPS) is a novel non-invasive brain stimulation technique with promising neuromodulation effects. No studies have examined target-specific deep brain TPS. This study assessed whether TPS of the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC) and anterior insular cortex (AIC) modulates risk-taking behavior and brain circuits in healthy participants. Methods Seventy-five healthy adults were randomized in this subjects/raters-blind study to 10 sessions of active dACC-TPS, active AIC-TPS, or sham-TPS over 2 weeks. Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART), a psychological measure of risk-taking behavior with high ecological validity, was assessed at baseline, midpoint (Week 1), and endpoint (Week 2). Resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) was measured at baseline and endpoint. Results Most participants experienced mild-to-moderate adverse events, primarily tingling and pain at the stimulation site. The overall dropout rate was 4%. Significant interactions emerged in the BART: dACC-TPS significantly decreased average pumps (average pumps on all trials), AIC-TPS significantly increased adjusted average pumps (average pumps on trials where the balloon did not burst), and sham showed no change. Target-specific rsFC changes were observed following active stimulation versus sham: dACC-TPS predominantly enhanced rsFC of dACC and AIC with precuneus, parietal, and occipital cortices, whereas AIC-TPS decreased rsFC of AIC with striatum. Conclusions Ten sessions of dACC-TPS and AIC-TPS are feasible and safe. dACC-TPS decreased risk-taking behavior, whereas AIC-TPS increased it. Bidirectional, target-specific rsFC changes were observed. Future large-scale studies with online neuroimaging or neurophysiological investigations are needed to confirm short- and long-term efficacy and clarify underlying mechanisms. Trial Registration ClinicalTrial.gov Identifier NCT06635161.

papers.title: A self-organized QTPat-based feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of English- and Turkish-associated EEG signals.
papers.authors: Yildiz AM, Keles T, Eris M, Barua PD, Baygin M, Tasci B, Taşcı İ, Dogan S, Tuncer T, Algul FE, Tan RS, Devi A, Acharya UR.
papers.abstract: Our primary aim is to develop an automated feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of EEG recordings acquired from English-speaking and Turkish-speaking participant cohorts. Drawing inspiration from a quantum tunnel pattern called QTPat, we introduced a novel approach of dynamically generating directed graphs to extract textural features. For our experiments, we utilized an EEG dataset containing 1652 English sentence-EEG pairs and 1600 Turkish sentence-EEG pairs. These signals were recorded from 20 English-speaking and 20 Turkish subjects who were presented with standardized sentences in their respective native languages. During the experiments, the participants were instructed to carefully contemplate each sentence while wearing a mobile brain cap system that acquired 14-channel EEG signals. Our preprocessing pipeline involved subjecting the EEG signals to multiple filtered wavelet packet decompositions, using both 6 Daubechies and 6 symlet wavelet filters. Subsequently, we extracted textural and statistical features employing the QTPat model, along with 20 statistical moments. To enhance discriminative power, we applied neighborhood component analysis and the Chi2-function to select the most relevant features. The k-nearest neighbor classifier was then employed to calculate predictive vectors. To further refine the results, we introduced an iterative hard majority voting scheme, generating additional voted vectors. Finally, we utilized a greedy algorithm to select the best-channel-wise and overall model results. Using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO CV), the proposed framework achieved 96.37% classification accuracy using four selected EEG channels. These findings demonstrate that the QTPat-based architecture can discriminate the two language-associated EEG cohorts under subject-independent evaluation. However, because language and participant population are coupled in the available dataset, the present results should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of language-specific neural decoding. Further studies using within-subject bilingual experimental designs are required to determine whether the identified EEG patterns specifically reflect language-related neural processing.

papers.title: Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination: Prediction of neurodevelopmental delay in children born between 29 and 36 weeks of gestation.
papers.authors: Brabant L, Dehaes M, Dufour MK, Gagnon MM, Belval V, Bernard C, Gagnon M, Côté-Corriveau G, Luu TM, Simard MN.
papers.abstract: Aim To evaluate the ability of the Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination (HINE) at 3 months 2 weeks corrected age to identify developmental difficulties at 2 years corrected age in infants born preterm between 29 and 36 weeks of gestation. Method In this prospective cohort study, the HINE was administered at 3 months 2 weeks corrected age. Development was assessed at 2 years corrected age using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4) and MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories. Developmental delay was defined using Bayley-4 scores less than 1 SD below the mean; expressive language delay was defined as a score less than the 10th centile for the number of spoken words expected for age. The cohort was largely free of brain lesions typically associated with cerebral palsy (5% intraventricular hemorrhage, with no other major brain lesions reported). Associations were examined using linear regression, screening performance using receiver operating characteristic curves, and incremental predictive value by comparing adjusted R2 across models, including perinatal and socioenvironmental factors with and without the HINE. Results A total of 174 infants were included in the analyses. The HINE total score was not associated with motor, cognitive, or language outcomes. Discriminative performance was poor (area under the curve = 0.48-0.57); adding the HINE total score to models including perinatal and socioenvironmental factors did not improve predictive performance. Interpretation A single HINE at 3 months 2 weeks corrected age has limited utility for identifying mild-to-moderate developmental difficulties in this population and should not be used alone to determine developmental surveillance needs. Longitudinal surveillance incorporating complementary sources of developmental, clinical, and socioenvironmental information may be more effective.

papers.title: Altered intrinsic neural timescales in cocaine use disorder.
papers.authors: Tang X, Di T, Sheng J, Sun Y, Zhang M, Luo W.
papers.abstract: Cocaine use disorder (CUD) is a major public health challenge, but its neurodynamic and molecular mechanisms remain unclear despite evidence of structural and functional abnormalities. This study mapped whole-brain intrinsic neural timescales (INTs), reflecting temporal integration of neural activity, using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging in 44 CUD patients and 44 healthy controls. In the primary analysis with global signal regression (GSR), CUD showed increased network-level INTs in the visual, somatomotor, dorsal attention, frontoparietal control, and default mode networks compared with HC. In the sensitivity analysis without GSR, the visual and somatomotor network differences remained significant. Within the CUD group, regional and network-level INT variation was associated with individual differences in flanker-task performance, despite the absence of significant between-group differences in behavioral performance. Notably, the spatial distribution of INT differences was associated with normative maps of gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptors and the noradrenaline transporter. Atlas-based models showed modest discrimination and limited validation, while outcome-informed cluster-based models yielded higher but exploratory estimates. Importantly, classification performance in a mixed-source evaluation sample was close to chance, indicating limited generalizability. Together, these findings reveal widespread alterations in intrinsic neural timescales in CUD and highlight the relevance of spatiotemporal brain organization to addiction.

papers.title: CAG repeat length shapes bidirectional functional connectome alterations in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3: a multimodal MRI study.
papers.authors: Yang X, Xia H, Hu Y, Xu C, Wang X, Deng Q, Xie Q, Dai L, Yang Q, Li C, Gui L, Liu C.
papers.abstract: The ATXN3 gene is the primary driver of brain damage in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3). We aimed to elucidate the patterns of connectome alterations shaped by cytosine-adenine-guanine (CAG) repeat length in SCA3. Eighty-nine genetically confirmed patients with SCA3 and 89 age-, sex-, education-matched healthy controls underwent multimodal MRI and comprehensive clinical assessments. Connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) was used to identify functional connectivity patterns associated with CAG repeat length. Structural brain damage was assessed using voxel-based morphometry. Mediation analysis was performed to examine the role of structural impairment in connectivity changes. CPM identified a positive and a negative network, whose connectivity strength increased or decreased with CAG repeat length. The positive network (r = 0.397, P < 0.001) was mainly localized within the cerebello-motor circuit and was positively associated with ataxia severity and functional disability. The negative network (r = 0.243, P = 0.022) was distributed across large-scale networks, with selective vulnerability of interhemispheric connectivity, and was associated with motor dysfunction. Besides the canonical motor pathways, limbic-related connectivity was related to motor impairment. Structural analyses revealed widespread gray matter atrophy centered on the cerebellum. Cerebellar atrophy statistically mediated the association between CAG repeat length and connectivity decreases. CAG repeat length is associated with a bidirectional connectopathy in SCA3. Cerebellar atrophy may mediate the connectivity decreases. Future longitudinal studies are required to examine the underlying causal pathway.

papers.title: Adaptive local region super-resolution for high-field MRI: A diffusion-based approach with structural and frequency-domain constraints.
papers.authors: Zuo J, Yang H, Tang Y, Wang X, Zhong K, Peng X, Luo J.
papers.abstract: High-field MRI offers superior SNR but is constrained by the trade-off between spatial resolution and acquisition time. Existing global deep learning super-resolution (SR) methods often incur computational overhead by ignoring regional image content. This motivates an adaptive local SR strategy to optimize efficiency and detail preservation. To address this, we developed a local SR method that adaptively allocates computational resources to information-rich regions. The proposed framework regularized an entropy-based local region processing strategy with a diffusion model fortified by frequency-domain and structural constraints.
