In this stratified 2×2 design, 70 participants, including individuals with ASD (n=35) and TD controls (n=35), will each be randomly assigned to either the verum or sham acupuncture group, resulting in 4 groups. The verum acupuncture group will receive stimulation at specific acupoints clinically indicated for ASD, eliciting a deqi sensation. The sham acupuncture group will receive superficial needling at nonacupoints unrelated to ASD symptoms. Each group will undergo clinical assessments and multimodal neuroimaging measurements, including functional near-infrared spectroscopy and electroencephalography, before and after acupuncture stimulation. The primary outcome will be differences in resting state network metrics and relative band power in frontal areas by disease status. Secondary outcomes will include differences in these neural markers following acupuncture stimulation between the verum and sham groups, reflecting the group × intervention interaction. Exploratory outcomes will focus on identifying neural markers that correlate with clinical indicators of ASD. Results Recruitment began in April 2025. To date, 23 individuals with ASD and 21 TD individuals have participated in this study. The recruitment process is expected to continue until December 2026. Conclusions ASD presents a significant socioeconomic burden, with no definitive treatment established to date. Although acupuncture is a widely applied intervention for various neurological conditions, including ASD, its large-scale neural mechanisms remain poorly understood. By using multimodal neuroimaging, the present study aims to investigate the immediate neural substrates underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD. These findings are expected to provide a robust neurobiological foundation for future longitudinal research and the development of evidence-based integrative strategies.

papers.title: Effective Connectivity and Clinical Correlates in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.authors: Han KI, Bae JH, Jo HJ, Park JM, Yeo Y, Park TS, Park DW, Kim TH.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.abstract: Background Cognitive impairment is a substantial comorbidity in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the neural mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. This study aimed to assess alterations in effective connectivity (EC) in patients with COPD and investigate their relationships with clinical measures. Methods Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (RS-fMRI) was performed in 38 patients with COPD and 30 healthy controls. EC was estimated using vector autoregressive (VAR) modelling combined with Granger causality analysis across 26 prespecified brain regions of interest derived from our previous functional connectivity study of the same cohort. Between-group differences in directed connectivity were assessed using Welch's t -tests. Associations between EC measures showing between-group differences and clinical measures were evaluated using age-adjusted partial Pearson correlations. Results At the nominal two-sided p < 0.05 level, 37 directed connections showed between-group differences in effective connectivity, and the mean vector autoregressive coefficients for 35 of these connections lay on opposite sides of zero between the COPD and control groups. Among the connections showing between-group differences, age-adjusted associations in patients with COPD involved pulmonary function, systemic oxygenation, cognition, affect, and health status. These associations involved distributed cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions, with several directed connections showing convergence across multiple clinical domains. Conclusion Resting-state VAR-based EC revealed distributed between-group differences in direction-sensitive BOLD temporal organization in COPD. Several of these EC measures were associated with pulmonary function, SpO2 , respiratory and COPD symptom burden, cognition, affect, and health status after age adjustment. These findings extend the functional connectivity profile of COPD by linking directed temporal relationships to its multidimensional clinical burden.

papers.title: EEG microstate-source coupling is spatially preserved in ALS
papers.authors: Metzger M, Costa G, Dukic S, McMackin R, Giglia E, Mitchell M, Bista S, Tadjine Y, Sirenko V, Plaitano S, Coffey A, Sharp AF, Mehra P, Suleyman N, Woods E, Heverin M, Bede P, Muthuraman M, Pender N, Hardiman O, Nasseroleslami B.
papers.abstract: Abstract EEG microstates are thought to reflect rapid transitions between brain-wide states and show disrupted temporal dynamics across neurological and psychiatric conditions, including ALS, yet the neural sources generating these states remain incompletely understood. Here, we introduce a source-resolved framework that links time-resolved microstate activations to estimated regional brain signals, enabling estimation of the neural sources underlying canonical microstate classes. Resting-state EEG from a large cohort of healthy controls (HC, n = 122) and individuals with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, n = 121) was analysed. Canonical microstates were derived from pooled data, and time-resolved microstate activation time series were estimated via projection-based decomposition of scalp potentials. In parallel, EEG source activity was reconstructed using beamformer-based inverse modelling and parcellated into 90 cortical regions. Microstate-source coupling was quantified using ridge regression linking microstate activations to reconstructed regional timecourses, producing spatially resolved coupling maps for each microstate class. In HC, reproducible and spatially distinct microstate-source coupling patterns were observed, consistent with structured mapping between scalp-defined brain states and distributed neural systems. Spatial reproducibility was confirmed using permutation-based null models that preserved temporal autocorrelation within microstate sequences and accounted for spatial dependence across regions. In HC, microstate-source coupling was spatially reproducible across independent subgroups for the four canonical microstates (A-D; r ≥ 0.90, q < 0.05). In ALS, coupling topography was preserved relative to HC for all four microstate classes (r ≥ 0.90, q < 0.05), and cluster-based permutation testing revealed no significant group differences in coupling magnitude for any microstate class, a null result robust to sex and riluzole status. Microstate-source coupling was preserved, suggesting stability of canonical microstate organisation across sensor and source space. Overall, these findings demonstrate that canonical EEG microstates have stable, reproducible coupling with distributed brain sources, and that this coupling organisation is preserved in ALS despite known alterations in microstate temporal characteristics. This dissociation suggests that spatial and temporal organisation of microstates may be governed by partially independent mechanisms, with spatial organisation buffered against ALS-related change, potentially through degeneracy or local compensatory mechanisms, while temporal engagement remains more directly sensitive to disease.

papers.title: Functional and Structural Imaging Features of Cognitive Profiles in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.authors: Jain K, Valsasina P, Mistri D, Meani A, Preziosa P, Filippi M, Rocca MA.
papers.abstract: Background and objectives Cognitive impairment affects 40%-70% of patients with multiple sclerosis (MS). Although recent hypothesis-driven and data-driven efforts have identified cognitive phenotypes, functional substrates underlying impairment in such phenotypes are still not clear. Our objective was to identify distinct cognitive phenotypes using clustering in a large cohort of patients with MS and characterize their associated clinical, structural MRI, and resting-state (RS) functional connectivity (FC) features. Methods We conducted an observational, cross-sectional study with right-handed patients with MS and age-matched and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) who underwent neurologic and neuropsychological evaluation (Brief Repeatable Battery of Neuropsychological tests). Latent profile analysis on cognitive test Z-scores identified MS cognitive phenotypes. 3.0T MRI was used to derive atrophy measures and RS FC within default mode network (DMN I/II), executive control network (ECN), left/right fronto-parietal, language, and salience networks. Linear regression models compared structural MRI and RS FC across cognitive phenotypes and HCs, while polynomial contrasts assessed RS FC patterns across groups. Results Three hundred and sixty-nine patients with MS and 168 HCs were enrolled. Four cognitive phenotypes were detected: preserved cognition ([PC], n = 67[18.2%]), mild single-domain verbal fluency involvement (MSD-VF, n = 37[10.0%]), mild single-domain attention involvement (MSD-A, n = 197[53.4%]), and severe multidomain (SMD) involvement (SMD, n = 68[18.4%]). At corrected threshold, PC patients showed decreased deep gray matter (GM) volumes (p < 0.001-0.001) and similar RS FC vs HCs, whereas MSD-VF exhibited no significant atrophy and no differences in RS FC vs HCs. MSD-A displayed lower cortical/deep GM volumes vs HCs (p < 0.001-0.005), whereas SMD had worse clinical and atrophy features (p < 0.001-0.04), as well as decreased DMN II RS FC (p = 0.01-0.04) vs other groups. Polynomial contrast analyses revealed significant quadratic patterns with increased RS FC in MSD-VF vs HC/PC groups, followed by decrease in MSD-A and SMD, within DMN II (p = 0.005), ECN (p = 0.005), and language network (p < 0.001). Discussion PC exhibited intact RS FC, whereas SMD presented widespread structural and DMN RS FC damage. These findings advance our understanding of cognitive heterogeneity in MS by revealing distinct structural and functional neuroimaging profiles across cognitive phenotypes, encouraging future longitudinal and multimodal investigations to improve disease characterization and prognostic stratification.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence EEG biomarkers for schizophrenia diagnosis: Systematic review with PROBAST+AI assessment.
papers.authors: Łoś K, Waszkiewicz N.
papers.journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists
papers.abstract: Background The application of artificial intelligence (AI) to resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) data represents a burgeoning frontier in schizophrenia diagnostics. However, the inferential validity of findings is frequently compromised by methodological heterogeneity. This systematic review rigorously evaluates the diagnostic efficacy and methodological robustness of AI-generated EEG biomarkers by implementing the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool for Artificial Intelligence (PROBAST+AI). Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified 43 primary studies encompassing 3,420 patients with schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis and 3,164 healthy controls (total N = 6,584). Methodological quality and validation strategies were assessed using the 34 signaling questions of the PROBAST+AI framework. Results The aggregate mean diagnostic accuracy across the literature was 93.38%, with deep learning architectures demonstrating superior metrics relative to classical machine learning (96.83% vs. 87.68%). Critically, external validation was restricted to 4.7% of the included studies. A pronounced performance discrepancy was observed between subject-wise (88.22%) and segment-wise (98.14%) validation protocols, indicating pervasive data leakage. Overall, 76.7% of the analyzed studies were characterized by a high risk of bias, predominantly stemming from suboptimal data partitioning and inadequate independent verification. Conclusions Contemporary diagnostic accuracies appear to be artifactually elevated due to structural methodological deficiencies and data leakage. Consequently, current evidence does not support the immediate clinical implementation of AI-EEG biomarkers in schizophrenia. To facilitate translational progress, we propose a standardized methodological framework optimizing validation strategies.

papers.title: Evidence for hierarchical representations of written and spoken words from an open-science human neuroimaging dataset.
papers.authors: Banerjee S, Jin K, Nikolov P, Cho P, Pendri VR, Chang L, Damera SR, Riesenhuber M.
papers.abstract: Reading and speech recognition rely on multi-level processing that builds from basic visual or sound features to complete word representations, yet details of these processing hierarchies (in particular those for spoken words) are still poorly understood. We re-analyzed the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data provided in the Mother Of all Unification Studies (MOUS) open-science dataset by using parametric regressions of word frequency and sublexical unit (bigram or syllable) frequency during reading and speech listening tasks in order to elucidate lexical and sublexical processing stages in the visual and auditory modalities. We first validated our approach in the written word domain, where the technique identified significant correlations for word frequency in the left mid-fusiform cortex (at the location of the Visual Word Form Area) and a left occipital region tracking bigram frequency, compatible with prior reports. During listening, activity in a left mid-superior temporal region consistent with the recently described Auditory Word Form Area (AWFA) showed a lexical frequency effect, while a more posterior region of the superior temporal gyrus was sensitive to syllable frequency. Activation in the left inferior frontal gyrus correlated with both written and spoken word frequencies. These findings suggest analogous posterior-to-anterior hierarchical organizations in the anteroventral visual and auditory streams, with modality-specific posterior sublexical and more anterior lexical representations that converge in higher-order language areas.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究重新分析开放科学脑成像数据，用词汇与亚词汇频率的参数回归比较阅读和听词的加工层级。结果在书写词中复现了视觉词形区的词汇频率效应及枕区对双字频的追踪；听词时听觉词形区呈词汇频率效应，更后部颞上回对音节频率敏感，左额下回与两种词频均相关。作者据此提出视觉与听觉腹侧通路存在类似的后到前层级组织，后部加工亚词汇、前部加工词汇，并在高级语言区汇聚。

papers.title: Validating the standard model of diffusion MRI in white matter with numerical substrates.
papers.authors: Nguyen-Duc J, Uhl Q, Oliveira R, Rafael-Patiño J, Jelescu IO.
papers.abstract: The non-invasive estimation of intra- and extracellular microstructural parameters using biophysical models has been a major focus in brain microstructure imaging with MRI. The Standard Model (SM) of diffusion in white matter (WM) provides a unifying framework for various modelling approaches, representing axons as impermeable sticks embedded within a locally anisotropic extra-axonal space. However, the SM relies on simplifying assumptions that may not hold in realistic WM tissue, as they do not take into account axonal undulations, beading, the presence of glial cells, or membrane permeability. In this work, we investigate how SM parameter estimates, derived using the Standard Model Imaging (SMI) framework, behave when the model is applied to realistic numerical WM substrates generated by the CATERPillar tool. Specifically, we vary (i) axonal morphological features such as beading and undulations, (ii) axonal packing density, (iii) orientation dispersion, (iv) membrane permeability of axons and astrocytes separately, (v) myelin volume fraction, and (vi) diffusion time. In each part of the analysis, different noise levels are introduced. Our findings enable users to identify potential biases introduced by varying conditions and to adjust their interpretations accordingly.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究检验白质扩散磁共振标准模型在更接近真实组织的数值底物上是否仍能给出可靠参数估计。作者用数值工具生成白质底物，改变轴突形态、堆积密度、方向弥散、膜通透性、髓鞘体积分数和扩散时间，并加入不同噪声水平，考察标准模型成像所得参数如何随之偏移。结果显示，这些简化假设未覆盖的因素会引入可识别的估计偏差，提示使用者需结合具体条件解读参数，而非将其直接视为真实微观结构的无偏读数。

papers.title: Altered prefrontal suppression of striatal activity during intrusive images in obsessive-compulsive disorder.
papers.authors: Vandevelde A, Dollfus S, Gagnepain P.
papers.abstract: Background Current models of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) emphasize dysfunction in frontostriatal circuits that support flexible behavioral control, leading to impulsive and compulsive actions. However, how these disruptions contribute to obsessions and intrusive thoughts remains poorly understood. Clarifying these mechanisms is essential for understanding cognitive control deficits in OCD. Method We examined intrusive memories elicited by emotional and neutral scenes in individuals with OCD (N = 24) and healthy controls (N = 21). Participants learned scene-cue associations and were later instructed to suppress memory retrieval when presented with reminder cues. Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) measured neural activity during suppression. Generalization of findings with alternative materials was assessed in larger samples of healthy controls (N = 73) and individuals with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD; N = 55). Results fMRI analyses showed preserved activity in frontoparietal, basal ganglia, and limbic regions in individuals with OCD, even during emotional intrusion suppression. However, unlike healthy controls, individuals with OCD failed to suppress striatal activity during intrusive memory, regardless of emotional content. Connectivity analyses indicated that this hyperactivity reflected reduced top-down inhibitory control, a disruption associated with greater obsessive symptom severity. Test of generalizability confirmed the role of frontostriatal downregulation in controlling intrusive thoughts and showed that this alteration was specific to OCD. Conclusions These findings emphasize the central role of frontostriatal circuits in regulating intrusive thinking. Obsessions in OCD may result from disrupted inhibitory mechanisms that normally restrict access to striatal-dependent information, contributing to persistent intrusive thoughts.

papers.title: Neuronavigated dual-target transcranial magnetic stimulation for schizophrenia negative symptoms.
papers.authors: Wei Y, Wang J, Tang X, Qian Z, Xu L, Cui H, Song Y, Zhu H, Ju M, Long B, Zhai W, Zeng L, Jiao X, Lan X, Wei X, Tang Y, Wang J, Zhang T.
papers.abstract: Negative symptoms in schizophrenia severely impair function and quality of life, yet respond poorly to current therapies. This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial aimed to investigate the efficacy of neuronavigated dual-target repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (rDLPFC) and cerebellum for improving negative symptoms in early-stage psychosis (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04853485). Participants with first-episode schizophrenia or clinical high-risk for psychosis were enrolled from Shanghai Mental Health Center and Suzhou Guangji Hospital. Participants were randomly assigned to either a real or sham group under MRI-guided neuronavigation, targeting rDLPFC with 1Hz at 100% motor threshold(MT), cerebellar with intermittent theta burst stimulation(iTBS) at 120% MT for 20 consecutive days. Clinical assessments were conducted at baseline(T0), 10-session(T1), 20-session(T2) and one month after the intervention(T3). Cognition and MRI were evaluated at T0 and T2. The primary outcome was change of negative subscale score of the Positive and Negative Symptoms Scale(PANSS), while secondary outcomes included alterations in other PANSS subscale scores and fronto-cerebellar circuit functional connectivity. In total, 75 participants were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (36 active, 39 sham). The pre-specified primary linear mixed-effects analysis revealed a non-significant group-by-time interaction for PANSS negative subscale scores (F(3,174.6)=1.45, p=0.230). At the 4-week endpoint (T2), the nominal unadjusted between-group p-value was 0.049; after Sidak correction for multiple comparisons, the adjusted mean difference was -2.48 points (95% CI -4.99 to 0.03, adjusted p=0.150, Cohen's d=-0.51). Descriptive uncorrected t-tests indicated greater negative-symptom reductions in the active group at T1 and T2, and the 4-week negative-symptom response rate (≥50% reduction) was higher under real rTMS (χ2=9.5, p=0.002). A significant group-by-time interaction was observed for PANSS positive subscale scores (F(3,172.0)=3.26, p=0.023). Both groups exhibited substantial within-group symptom improvement. Resting-state fMRI demonstrated group-by-time interactions within cerebello-temporal, parahippocampal, caudate, and parietal networks (FWE-corrected p<0.05), and negative-symptom change correlated with cerebello-caudate connectivity (r=0.33, p=0.026). These findings suggest neuronavigated dual-target rTMS over rDLPFC and cerebellum may be associated with numerical improvements in negative symptoms in early-stage psychosis.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注导航下右侧背外侧前额叶与小脑双靶点重复经颅磁刺激能否改善早期精神病（首发精神分裂症或精神病临床高危）的阴性症状，采用多中心随机双盲假对照设计，真刺激组接受1Hz rDLPFC与iTBS小脑刺激共20天，主要结局为PANSS阴性分量表评分变化。意向性分析纳入75人（真刺激36、假刺激39），预设线性混合模型未发现显著的组×时间交互（p=0.230）；4周终点经Sidak校正后组间差异亦不显著（校正p=0.150），仅未校正检验和应答率提示真刺激组降幅更大，且两组均有明显组内改善。静息态fMRI显示小脑-颞叶、海马旁回、尾状核及顶叶网络存在组×时间交互，阴性症状变化与小脑-尾状核连接相关。作者据此仅提示该双靶点方案可能与阴性症状的数值性改善相关，未确立疗效。

papers.title: Pupil dilation as an index of episodic processing when remembering, imagining, and thinking creatively.
papers.authors: Thakral PP, Madore KP, Devitt AL.
papers.abstract: Prior research indicates that the cognitive and neural systems supporting the recall of specific past experiences (episodic memory) also play a key role in imagining novel and specific future experiences (episodic simulation), and divergent creative thinking. In particular, constructive memory processes (e.g. retrieval and recombination of specific episodic details) are thought to benefit episodic simulation and divergent thinking. In the current study, we provide a novel test of this hypothesis using eye-tracking. We capitalized on prior eye-tracking and neuroimaging evidence demonstrating that pupil dilation and hippocampal activity are enhanced when memory is associated with the retrieval of episodic detail relative to non-episodic detail. We tracked pupil dilation as participants recalled past experiences, imagined novel future experiences, engaged in divergent thinking, or performed a non-episodic/semantic retrieval task. Pupil dilation tracked divergent thinking ability and the number of episodic details generated during episodic memory and simulation. No relationship was observed between pupil dilation and performance in the semantic memory task, or the generation of non-episodic details during episodic memory and simulation. In contrast, fixation counts tracked performance in the semantic retrieval task. In line with prior findings, we interpret the results as reflecting the retrieval of specific information during episodic memory, simulation, and divergent thinking. At a broader level, these findings suggest that examining pupillometry is a promising direction for identifying common episodic processes.

papers.title: Two clusters of brain regions with distinct age-related profiles of functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder.
papers.authors: Li X, Zuo F, Cheng Y, Perkins K, Cao F.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Brain functional connectivity changes throughout development, and individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may follow trajectories that differ from those of typically developing controls. Using large multisite resting-state fMRI cross-sectional datasets, we examined how functional connectivity differences between ASD and typically developing controls change across a broad age range of 5 to 64 y. A data-driven analysis identified two spatially distributed clusters of cortical regions showing distinct age-related profiles of ASD-TD connectivity differences. Cluster 1 was marked by consistent hypoconnectivity across ages, suggesting a stable neural signature of ASD. Cluster 2 was characterized by hypoconnectivity in childhood that gradually diminished with age, suggesting a temporary delay profile. These clusters were systematically organized along the sensory-association axis. Cluster 1 mainly involved lower-rank sensory and sensorimotor cortices, while Cluster 2 mainly involved higher-rank association cortices. Brain-behavior analyses revealed greater and broader ASD symptom associations across ages in the consistent hypoconnectivity profile than the delay profile. Further subtype analyses suggested that social-affect symptoms were associated with greater hypoconnectivity than repetitive behavior symptoms in both clusters. Spatial correlation analyses with neurotransmitter maps revealed associations of Cluster 1 with mGluR5 and of Cluster 2 with GABAA α5, providing insight into the neurobiological basis of the two clusters. In a cross-disorder validation analysis, applying the same analytic framework to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder did not reveal comparable results. Together, these findings suggest that ASD-related functional connectivity alterations are developmentally heterogeneous and organized along the cortical hierarchy, providing a developmental perspective for understanding the neurobiology of ASD.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究利用多中心静息态功能磁共振横断面数据，考察5至64岁孤独症谱系障碍者与典型发育者之间功能连接差异如何随年龄变化。数据驱动分析识别出两个空间分布的皮层区域簇：一簇在各年龄段均表现为稳定的连接减弱，另一簇的连接减弱主要在童年出现并随年龄逐渐消退，呈延迟特征；两簇沿感觉—联合皮层轴组织，且稳定减弱簇与症状的关联更广更强。作者据此提出，孤独症相关功能连接改变在发育上具有异质性，并沿皮层等级组织。

papers.title: Mechanistic versus descriptive interpretation of brain activity pattern reconstruction.
papers.authors: Jung K, Eickhoff SB, Patil KR.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: The geometric eigenmodes, derived from the shape of the cortical surface, have been suggested as a better model for explaining brain function due to their high accuracy in reconstructing patterns of both spontaneous and stimulus-evoked brain activity patterns captured by functional MRI, when contrasted with alternative models including structural connectome derived bases. While a descriptive representation offers valuable utility for neuroimaging studies, it is necessary to examine the extent to which it supports a mechanistic explanation for human brain function. Although the observation that geometric eigenmodes accurately fit brain activity is intriguing, we argue that accepting them as a model of brain function risks conflating descriptive and mechanistic interpretations. While a representation that effectively describes the underlying geometry is inherently adept at fitting patterns within that geometric space; it does not necessarily shed light on mechanisms that give rise to the brain's functional attributes. To this end, we provide two lines of empirical results: a) geometric eigenmodes demonstrate a high flexibility when fit to a range of manipulated patterns, and b) localized parcel-based representations can reconstruct activity patterns as well. Based on those results, theoretical considerations, and previous data, we argue that more consideration is needed regarding the complementary roles of descriptive representation and mechanistic explanation in neuroimaging research. While we recognize the potential role of the brain's geometry in influencing its dynamics, assertions regarding its efficacy should be weighed against its inherent lack of specificity, biological interpretability, and anatomical evidence.
papers.summary_zh: 该文讨论用皮层表面几何本征模态重建脑活动模式时，描述性表征与机制性解释之间的混淆问题。作者以两项实证结果说明：几何本征模态对多种人为操纵的模式也能灵活拟合，而基于局部脑区的表征同样可重建活动模式。作者据此指出，几何本征模态拟合精度高并不等于揭示了脑功能的产生机制，其特异性、生物学可解释性和解剖学证据均有限，呼吁神经影像研究更审慎地区分描述与机制解释。

papers.title: Periventricular gradient pathology is linked to ependymal reactivity and cell adhesion disruption in multiple sclerosis.
papers.authors: Groh AMR, Afanasiev E, Thevakumaran R, Creeggan F, Callahan-Martin L, Bigotte M, Yaqubi M, Gertsvolf J, Pei J, Wu H, de Vos J, Aalders MCG, Zandee S, Prat A, Rudko DA, Stratton JA.
papers.abstract: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-adjacent brain areas are especially vulnerable to diffuse degeneration in multiple sclerosis (MS). Surface-in gradients arising from CSF-borne cytotoxic factors have been proposed to predict disease relapses independent of white matter lesions. Yet, whether such factors disrupt ependymal cells to penetrate the ventricular border in MS remains unknown. Here, using ultra-high-field magnetic resonance imaging-guided histology, electron microscopy and single-nucleus multiomics, we found that ependymal pathology correlates with periventricular gradients and involves an immune-reactive state marked by transporter and junctional protein dysregulation. We further defined the gene regulatory networks underpinning the MS ependymal state and predicted ligands known to be enriched in MS CSF that could drive the emergence of this state. One of the candidates, IFNγ, increased murine ependymal permeability in vivo, indicating that CSF ligands can modulate ependymal function and regional inflammation. These findings identify CSF-driven ependymal dysfunction as a contributor to periventricular pathology in MS.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注多发性硬化中脑室周围区域易受弥漫性退变影响的机制，特别是脑脊液来源因素是否通过破坏室管膜细胞而参与这一过程。作者结合超高场磁共振引导的组织学、电子显微镜和单核多组学方法，分析多发性硬化组织中的室管膜病理状态及其与脑室周围梯度的关联。研究发现室管膜病理与脑室周围梯度相关，表现为转运蛋白和连接蛋白失调的免疫反应状态，并构建了相应的基因调控网络、预测了脑脊液中可能驱动该状态的配体。候选配体IFNγ在体内可增加小鼠室管膜通透性，提示脑脊液配体能够调节室管膜功能与局部炎症，但该研究主要基于关联和组织/动物实验，尚不能确立临床因果关系。

papers.title: Polygenic scores for longevity in relation to brain MRI measures in a cohort of 70-year-olds.
papers.authors: Seidu NM, Lindberg O, Kern S, Rydén L, Wahlund LO, Waern M, Mohanty R, Cedres N, Zetterberg H, Blennow K, Erhag HF, Zettergren A, Westman E, Holstege H, Skoog I.
papers.abstract: Population-based studies on the relation between polygenic longevity scores (PGLSs) and specific brain regions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are few. We aimed to investigate this relationship in a population of 70-year-olds from Gothenburg, Sweden (N = 675). We constructed two PGLSs (one with and one without the APOE locus) using longevity GWAS summary statistics. MRI outcomes included total grey matter, white matter (WM), WM hyperintensities (WMHs), subcortical volumes, small vessel disease (SVD) score, cortical thicknesses, and fractional anisotropy (FA) fibre tracts. We adjusted for sex, age, principal components, and sex interactions, and corrected for multiple comparisons. We found no associations in the total sample. In males, both PGLSs were associated with smaller WMHs volume and lower SVD burden, and a thicker cortex of pars triangularis, pars opercularis, and insula. Our findings suggest a possible link between genetic propensity for longevity and lower cerebrovascular burden and certain cortical grey matter areas in males.

papers.title: Predicting individual differences in social functioning from functional connectomes in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.authors: Li A, Zhang J, Yu C, Tan L, Yi A, Xiao Y.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by profound heterogeneity in social functioning. While previous studies using group-level comparisons and predefined regions of interest have identified neural correlates of social deficits in ASD, the neural basis of individual differences in social functioning remains unclear. Here, we applied connectome-based predictive modeling to resting-state functional MRI data from 65 children with ASD aged 1.5-8 years (mean age = 4.23 years) to predict individual differences in social functioning assessed by the personal-social subscale of the Griffiths Development Scales (GDS). Results showed that whole-brain functional connectivity significantly predicted personal-social scores. The positive predictive network was dominated by connections within the default mode network, with the left precuneus emerging as a core hub. In contrast, the negative predictive network mainly involved inter-network connections, particularly between the frontoparietal and sensorimotor networks. In an independent cohort of 27 children with ASD aged 1.25-8 years (mean age = 3.31 years), the positive-edge model showed a significant association with personal-social scores, whereas the negative-edge and combined models did not. These findings suggest that intrinsic large-scale brain network organization is associated with individual differences in social functioning in children with ASD, highlighting the potential of network-level approaches for characterizing neurodevelopmental heterogeneity and supporting future precision-oriented research.

papers.title: A comparative study of modified suanzaoren decoction versus estazolam in chronic insomnia disorder: Clinical outcomes and thalamocortical network changes.
papers.authors: Wang R, Han Y, Chen L, Lv D, Yao P, Guo Z, Guo W.
papers.abstract: Chronic insomnia disorder (CID) is associated with widespread abnormalities in thalamic functional connectivity (FC). For CID patients with the yin-deficiency and fire-excess syndrome, Modified Suanzaoren Decoction (MSZRD) and estazolam are common treatments, but their longitudinal associations with thalamic networks remain unclear. This study was a non-randomized, patient-preference controlled trial. Eighty-two CID patients with yin-deficiency and fire-excess syndrome received a 6-week treatment with either MSZRD or estazolam based on preference. Additionally, 54 healthy controls (HCs) were recruited for baseline comparison. Clinical scales, polysomnography, and resting-state fMRI data were collected pre- and post-treatment. Using the Human Brainnetome Atlas, the thalamus was parcellated into eight subregions. We examined baseline group differences and longitudinal FC changes, and identified genes associated with the baseline FC alterations for enrichment analysis. At baseline, CID patients showed significantly increased FC in pathways involving the medial pre-frontal thalamus, posterior parietal thalamus, lateral pre-frontal thalamus, and caudal temporal thalamus with multiple cortical regions. After treatment, the MSZRD group showed greater improvement than the estazolam group on subjective and objective measures. While FC decreased in the MSZRD group between the left occipital thalamus and right middle frontal gyrus, and between the right occipital thalamus and right angular gyrus, it increased in the estazolam group for these connections. Enrichment analysis of genes associated with baseline FC alterations identified pathways related to synaptic organization, cytoskeletal stability, and metabolism. These findings provide preliminary evidence that CID is associated with enhanced thalamocortical connectivity consistent with the thalamus-centric hyperarousal model, and that MSZRD and estazolam show different clinical and neural correlates. However, due to the non-randomized design and baseline FC differences, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in future randomized mechanistic studies.

papers.title: Peripheral pathway rerouting shapes whole-brain functional network.
papers.authors: Hu JJ, Xiang YT, Huo BB, Zuo YF, Peng CY, He-Wang, Wu JJ, Zheng MX, Xu JG.
papers.abstract: Pathway rerouting is critical for severe peripheral nerve injury (PNI), which induces widespread neuroplastic alterations within the central nervous system, yet whether different rerouting approaches differentially affect whole-brain functional networks remains unknown. The present study investigated alterations in brain network organization following different peripheral pathway rerouting after PNI. Adult Sprague-Dawley rats underwent complete left brachial plexus transection and were assigned to nerve repair, end-to-end nerve transfer, end-to-side nerve transfer, or untreated PNI groups. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging was acquired 7 months after surgery. Whole-brain functional connectivity matrices were constructed, and graph theoretical analysis was performed to assess global and nodal network properties, including global efficiency, nodal efficiency, and small-world characteristics. Rich-club, feeder, and local connections were further analyzed to characterize patterns of network reorganization. The results revealed significant differences in global efficiency, nodal efficiency, small-world organization and feeder connection among the four groups. Compared with the other reconstruction procedures, end-to-end nerve transfer showed reduced global efficiency, impaired small-world organization, lower nodal efficiency in subcortical regions, and increased functional connectivity and feeder connections, indicating reduced efficiency of large-scale information processing. In contrast, end-to-side nerve transfer preserved global efficiency, nodal efficiency, and small-world properties to a greater extent and was accompanied by more extensive increases in functional connectivity. These findings suggest that end-to-end nerve transfer appears to have a negative effect on the order of the whole-brain network, whereas end-to-side nerve transfer better preserves and restores network stability.

papers.title: A brainstem module for backward locomotion reveals direction-selective premotor circuits.
papers.authors: Liu Z, Lu L, Di R, Cui Y, Liu Y, Ren Q, Dai R, Wu W, Wang R, Luo M.
papers.abstract: Smooth locomotion requires precise directional control, yet the neural circuits governing navigational transitions remain elusive. Here, we identify the pontine backward locomotion center (PBLC) as a key brainstem node for backward locomotion in mice. PBLC glutamatergic neurons are preferentially recruited during backward locomotion; their activation elicits robust backward walking with naturalistic gait features, whereas their inhibition suppresses backward movement across multiple behavioral contexts. PBLC neurons send ascending projections to the peri-fasciculus retroflexus and descending projections to the paramedian reticular nucleus (PMn). Activating spinal-projecting PMn glutamatergic neurons evokes backward locomotion, whereas PMn ablation suppresses PBLC-evoked backward movement. The PBLC lies within an anteroposteriorly organized set of brainstem regions that includes the cuneiform nucleus, ventral laterodorsal tegmental nucleus, and lateral parabrachial nucleus, associated with forward locomotion, ipsilateral turning, and locomotor arrest, respectively. Together, these findings define a supraspinal circuit for backward locomotion and reveal neighboring brainstem modules associated with distinct locomotor actions.

papers.title: The legible body and the language of cognition.
papers.authors: Mainen ZF.
papers.abstract: Neural activity moves the body to act on the world, and the world returns through the body to shape neural activity. Systems neuroscience built tasks to cut this loop, isolating low-dimensional, task-related signals and discarding the rest. Tasks suited cognition as classically conceived: general-purpose machinery between sensation and action, performing latent computations abstracted from specific behaviors. With recording techniques limited to tracking individual neurons and discrete actions, it took tasks to make cognition legible by supplying meaning within a limited but generalizable frame. That constraint has been lifting: brain-wide neural recording and rich video tracking of the body can now read neurons and behavior as two facets of one dynamical system. Together they reveal cognitive primitives - decision variables, expected values, hidden states - distributed not only in brain activity but also in subtle face and body movements long dismissed as noise. Cognition, it turns out, is not confined to higher-order cortex; it surfaces in incidental movements carrying latent variables the brain computes - even ones it never acts on. It keeps its hold on the body, as emotion keeps its expressions. Backed by normative theories, noninvasive video recordings can divulge not only the syntax of behavior but also its semantics, opening the study of cognition in the wild beyond tasks. The potential is perhaps greatest in our own species, where the promise of reading the mind noninvasively - to treat and to understand - is mirrored by the threat of laying it bare.

papers.title: Cross-cohort transfer of clinical Alzheimer's EEG signatures to cognitively healthy APOE-ε4 and PICALM rs3851179 risk carriers using differentiable logic gate networks.
papers.authors: Dharia SY, Valderrama CE, Smith SD.
papers.abstract: Neural alterations associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD) may emerge years before clinical diagnosis, and genetic risk factors such as APOE-ε4 and PICALM rs3851179 may identify individuals vulnerable to these shifts. We tested whether electroencephalography (EEG) signatures learned from clinically diagnosed AD patients transfer to cognitively healthy middle-aged adults carrying these variants. Differentiable logic gate networks (Diff-Logic) and neural baselines were trained on log-relative power spectral density features from a clinical cohort of AD patients and cognitively normal (CN) controls. These models were then applied without retraining to an independent genetic-risk cohort of neutral-risk non-carriers (N), APOE-ε4-only carriers (A+P-), and dual APOE-ε4/PICALM G-allele carriers (A+P+), yielding a continuous AD-like EEG signature score per participant. Diff-Logic matched neural baselines in clinical classification (balanced accuracy 0.809±0.028; AUROC 0.845±0.023) while enabling edge inference with a 7.4× model-size reduction and 0.22 ms model-only latency on a 7 W single-core CPU. In the genetic-risk cohort, scores were highest in A+P+ participants (0.393±0.167) relative to N (0.296±0.154) and A+P- (0.285±0.143; subject-level mean ± SD). This elevation was nominally significant before correction (A+P+ vs. A+P-, punc =0.036) but did not survive Holm correction (pHolm =0.109), and the cohort carried no AD pathology or conversion ground truth; the association was therefore exploratory. Integrated gradients attribution of the trained model showed genetic-risk relevance in delta, theta, and alpha, partially overlapping clinical AD topography. These findings support the feasibility of zero-shot EEG transfer in genetically at-risk individuals and highlight the need for replication in larger cohorts. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/Shyamal-Dharia/ad-difflogic-transfer.

papers.title: Caffeine Consumption and Adolescent Mental Health: The Role of Sleep and Brain Structure.
papers.authors: Zheng J, Rakesh D.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
papers.abstract: Background Caffeine is a widely consumed psychoactive substance, with use beginning during adolescence, a sensitive period of neurodevelopment. Despite its widespread, unregulated use, links between caffeine consumption and adolescent brain structure and mental health remain poorly understood. Methods We examined the association between caffeine intake and brain structure in 9632 adolescents aged 9-11 years. Caffeine consumption (intake of coffee, tea and soft drinks) and mental health were assessed via self-report. Cortical thickness and surface area were derived from structural MRI scans. Linear mixed-effects models tested associations between caffeine intake and brain measures. Structural equation modeling was used to test whether sleep duration and brain structure mediated the association between caffeine intake and mental health outcomes assessed at the 6-month and 18-month follow-up. Results Higher total caffeine intake was associated with lower total cortical surface area (B=-0.03,SE=0.01,p=.001) and lower surface area in 22 regions across four lobes, driven largely by soft drink consumption, with some additional associations emerging for coffee and espresso intake with cortical thickness. All associations were evident at consumption levels as low as one cup per week. Shorter sleep duration and lower surface area sequentially mediated the association between higher caffeine intake and greater mental health problems in the future. Conclusion Findings highlight the need for evidence-based guidelines on adolescent caffeine consumption to support neurodevelopment and mental health.

papers.title: Air-jet Pneumodissection in Neuroanatomy: a new method for the study of White Matter anatomy in the Human Brain.
papers.authors: Marrone S, Scalia G, De Notaris M, Corrivetti F, Umana GE.
papers.abstract: Traditional white matter (WM) dissection techniques, such as the Klingler method, employ wooden or metal instruments that may cause myelin wear and limit fine anatomical separation. Inspired by clinical water-jet applications, we investigated the feasibility of an air-jet dissector (pneumodissection) for WM dissection, leveraging the Coandă effect to gently separate contiguous fiber tracts while preserving their integrity. A portable air compressor was modified with an extended tube and an 18G blunt needle tip. A left cerebral hemisphere, prepared according to a modified Klingler freeze-thaw protocol, was dissected under exoscope magnification. Airflow was delivered at pressures between 0.8 and 3 bar. Dissection followed Klingler's stepwise protocol, adapted to the ergonomics and dynamics of the air-jet device. The air-jet dissector enabled progressive detachment of pia-arachnoid membranes, cortex and U-fibers, with clear exposure of commissural, projection, and association bundles. Low-pressure flow (0.8-1.2 bar) was used for delicate superficial planes and U-shaped fibers, whereas transient increases up to 3 bar were used for more resistant cortical or deep tissue planes. During this feasibility experiment, the air jet reduced broad direct instrument-tissue contact and helped clear loose debris and surface fluid from the operative field. Vessel-fiber interfaces and anatomical cleavage planes were sharply delineated. The device's portability and pressure modulation allowed both blunt and sharp dissection functions through a single tool. Air-jet dissection is a novel and complementary technique for white matter study. The present study does not establish superiority or reduced tissue damage compared with conventional manual tools because no matched quantitative comparison or histological assessment was performed. Further replicated and standardized studies are required to define reproducibility, tissue effects, and any objective advantage over established dissection methods.

papers.title: Improved diffusion tensor parametric maps in the brain from reduced-direction acquisitions using a deep learning approach.
papers.authors: Tucksinapinunchai N, Boonsuth R, Rodkong A, Saokhieo P, Peragine DE, Skorska MN, Thurston LT, Hu DZ, Supindham T, Kaewthip O, Wantanajittikul K, Saekho S, Chariyalertsak S, Angkurawaranon S, VanderLaan DP, Yarach U.
papers.abstract: Objectives This study implements and evaluates a deep learning approach to enhance FA, MD, AD, and RD maps derived from 16-direction DTI to approximate corresponding maps derived from 32-direction DTI, with the aim of reducing acquisition time while maintaining quantitative accuracy. Materials and methods A modified 8-layer 3D convolutional neural network was trained using scalar DTI-derived maps from 16-direction acquisitions as input and corresponding 32-direction maps as reference targets. Model performance was evaluated on an independently acquired evaluation cohort (n=33) using PSNR, %NRMSE, SSIM, Bland-Altman analysis, and tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS), with BM4D and AONLM as comparators. Results The DL model reduced noise and improved PSNR, %NRMSE, and SSIM compared with raw ND16, BM4D, and AONLM (p < 0.05). DL-derived FA, MD, and AD showed the smallest deviations from the ND32 reference among the evaluated methods, although statistically significant mean differences remained. TBSS showed localized differences for FA and AD, but no significant differences for MD or RD (p > 0.05). Discussion The proposed map-domain DL approach improved scalar DTI-derived maps from 16-direction acquisitions while reducing diffusion acquisition time by approximately 1.8-fold. The findings demonstrate improved agreement with 32-direction reference maps, while remaining quantitative differences and generalizability require further validation.

papers.title: Impact of sedation on the reliability of magnetoencephalographic language mapping in pediatric epilepsy.
papers.authors: Song T, Song RR, Bodden C, Deleon R, Cordova J, Huang M, Calley C.
papers.abstract: Objective Magnetoencephalography (MEG) language mapping in pediatric epilepsy frequently requires sedation, which may alter cortical physiology and compromise the reliability of language lateralization. We hypothesized that sedation disrupts coupling between early auditory processing and higher order language networks, reducing the interpretability of laterality metrics. Methods Sixty-nine pediatric patients undergoing presurgical MEG evaluation were analyzed, including 32 nonsedated and 37 sedated participants. Auditory evoked field responses were quantified using the M200/M100 amplitude ratio and interhemispheric asymmetry. Language laterality indices (LIs) were derived from a continuous recognition memory paradigm, and source localization was performed using Fast-VESTAL. Results Sedation preferentially suppressed late auditory responses, reflected by a significant reduction in the M200/M100 ratio (p < .001) and increased interindividual variability. Despite preserved early sensory responses, auditory-language coupling was numerically attenuated under sedation. Notably, low M200/M100 ratios were frequently associated with highly lateralized LI values, suggesting reduced physiological reliability and the potential for "false certainty" in language lateralization. Source imaging demonstrated preserved primary auditory cortical activity with reduced recruitment of higher order association networks in sedated participants. Significance Sedation compromises the physiological reliability of MEG language lateralization by disrupting late auditory and association-level processing. The M200/M100 ratio provides a practical physiological marker for identifying cases in which laterality results should be interpreted with caution. These findings support a physiology-informed framework for improving the clinical interpretation of MEG language mapping in sedated pediatric patients, with direct implications for presurgical planning in pediatric epilepsy.

papers.title: Extensive Parenchymal Brain Calcification in a Patient With Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease and Stage 5 Chronic Kidney Disease.
papers.authors: Khan N, Streicher N.
papers.abstract: Extensive parenchymal brain calcification is uncommon in chronic kidney disease (CKD): intracranial vascular calcification affects up to 10% of uremic patients, but widespread Fahr-type parenchymal deposits are rare and, where reported, have occurred in patients with a coexisting hypoparathyroid or parathyroid-hormone (PTH)-resistant state. We describe a man in his 50s with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) and Stage 5 CKD who presented with word-finding difficulty, gait imbalance, and myoclonus and was found to have extensive symmetric calcification of the basal ganglia, thalami, dentate nuclei, and subcortical white matter. He carried an unverified childhood diagnosis of pseudohypoparathyroidism made at age 13. At presentation, total calcium was 6.1-6.3 mg/dL, phosphate 5.8 mg/dL, intact PTH 194 pg/mL, creatinine 6.21 mg/dL, and alkaline phosphatase normal. Over the following 10 months, intact PTH fell rather than rose, reaching 56 pg/mL during treatment with calcium, calcitriol, sevelamer, and hemodialysis, all of which lower PTH whatever the underlying cause. The calcium-phosphate product was low at presentation (36.5 mg2 /dL2 ) but rose to 58-62 mg2 /dL2 later, and single values cannot exclude earlier CKD-related mineral abnormality. No pathogenic variant was identified on an 866-gene panel. Neither the product nor the PTH trajectory separated renal from non-renal contributions. We present this as a diagnostic-reasoning case that raises, but cannot resolve, the question of causation and suggest that such calcification should not be attributed to CKD-mineral and bone disorder by default.

papers.title: Cross-state stability and maturational similarity of the social brain connectome in children and adolescents
papers.authors: Lee J, Eilbott J, Kelly C, Todd R, Vanderwal T.
papers.abstract: The intra-individual stability of functional connectivity (FC) across two or more scans and the inter-individual similarity of FC patterns relative to peers capture developmental variability in functional brain organization. Despite their different referents, these measures are strongly coupled at the whole brain level; however, it remains unclear whether this relationship emerges in development, whether it extends to the social brain, and whether it differs by sex. Based on the importance of social development in this age range, we hypothesized that known developmental relationships and sex-specific effects would be more pronounced in the social brain relative to the whole brain. Using a large psychiatrically enriched sample of 769 youth ages 6-21 (female N = 327, mean age = 12.27 years), we computed FC during rest and movie-watching scans and quantified stability across scans as well as similarity to mature subjects (n=36) within each condition. We then tested whether sex-dependent age relationships were captured by these measures or by the strength of their coupling. Our results showed that cross-state stability and maturational similarity are strongly coupled in development, and that this coupling is enhanced in the social brain relative to the whole brain. Furthermore, the strength of stability-similarity coupling increased as a function of age in females, while males showed the opposite effect. When assessing relationships between age and each FC measure independently, no individual effects were significant after FDR correction. However, our multivariate age-prediction models fared much better, demonstrating that edgewise stability and maturational similarity measures can capture spatially heterogeneous developmental effects that are lost when collapsing across edges. Together, these results support the emerging idea that the degree of FC stability across scans is related to how closely an individual’s functional architecture aligns to a shared template. Here, we newly show that this stability-similarity coupling is stronger in the social brain and varies with age in sex-specific ways. Future longitudinal work is needed to establish whether these cross-sectional relationships also characterize within-person developmental change.

papers.title: Virtual Brain Modelling Reveals Altered Network Dynamics and Predicts Symptom Severity in Schizophrenia: Relevance to Antipsychotic Treatment Response and Resistance
papers.authors: Vitacca M, Pischedda D, Ciccarelli M, Pontillo G, De Simone G, Cocozza S, Ćipranić F, Monteverdi A, Fusar-Poli P, Gandini Wheeler-Kingshott CAM, Palesi F, de Bartolomeis A, D’Angelo E.
papers.abstract: Background Schizophrenia (SZ) is a heterogeneous disorder characterized by positive, negative, cognitive and disorganisation symptoms, with pleomorphic phenotype and poorly understood aetiology. Dopamine dysregulation represents the most replicated in vivo pathophysiology finding. However, accumulating evidence suggests altered large-scale brain connectivity and excitation/inhibition balance disruption. While quantifying these alterations would help clarify SZ neurophysiology and guide therapy, single-patient identification remains impractical. This is particularly relevant for treatment-resistant SZ (TRS) whose pathophysiology remains unclear. Methods Using virtual brain modelling, we simulated large-scale brain dynamics from functional and structural MRI data in 43 healthy controls and 33 SZ patients, stratified into TRS and non-TRS. We used the Wong-Wang model to derive four network parameters reflecting GABAergic and NMDA receptor-mediated glutamatergic transmission: global coupling (G), local inhibitory (J i ) and excitatory (J NMDA ) coupling, and recurrent excitation (w + ). We performed simulations in the whole brain and in resting-state networks, compared model parameters between groups and tested their association with Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) scores. Results Compared to non-TRS, TRS patients showed increased J NMDA and decreased w + at the whole-brain level, increased J NMDA and G in the dorsal attention network, lower G in the limbic network and increased w + in the visual network. Moreover, J i in the default mode network predicted negative symptom severity while J NMDA in the limbic and ventral attention networks predicted total PANSS scores and disorganisation. Conclusions These findings suggest that TRS is characterized by network-specific alterations in excitation/inhibition profiles and support the use of personalised multiscale modelling to identify symptom biomarkers.

papers.title: Biologically inspired alignment reveals distributed and directionally asymmetric correspondence between rat and human cortices
papers.authors: Dong X, Luo Q, Cai A, Jin Z, Mu C, Wang F, Shan H.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rodent models enable causal interrogation of brain circuits, but translating their systems-level organization to humans requires correspondence beyond one-to-one anatomical homology. Guided by the view that cortical areas are characterized by their relationships within distributed functional networks, we developed BrainMapping, a biologically inspired framework for aligning rat and human cortex using resting-state functional MRI. The framework combined a shared representation with optimal transport to derive probabilistic, bidirectional maps. These alignments revealed distributed, many-to-many correspondences that generalized to held-out subjects and preserved functional connectivity architecture, cortical gradients, and graph topology. Organizational preservation was directionally asymmetric. Human-to-rat mapping preserved organization more uniformly across rat cortical systems, whereas rat-to-human mapping showed stronger preservation in human association-related networks than in primary sensory and motor networks. The maps recovered literature-consistent default-mode and salience-system correspondences and generated testable non-canonical predictions. These findings provide a framework for expressing rat functional organization in human functional-network coordinates.

papers.title: Differential subcortical-cortical circuit reorganization in autism and ADHD
papers.authors: Zhou G, Xie K, Ngo A, Ding R, Cabalo DG, Wang Y, Smith M, Nakamura M, Royer J, Serediuc N, Toussaint PJ, Mottron L, Martino AD, Milham MP, Hong S, Evans AC, Bernhardt BC.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often co-occur and share symptoms as well as genetic risk factors. While subcortical-cortical networks have been implicated in both conditions, particularly involving thalamic and striatal circuits, patterns of shared and diverging disruptions remain unclear. Here we integrated resting-state functional connectivity (FC) and regression dynamic causal modeling (rDCM) across a transdiagnostic multi-site cohort. We used statistical group comparisons and individualized normative deviation mapping to map network deviations in ASD and ADHD relative to neurotypical controls and against one another. Multivariate associative techniques examined associations to clinical and cognitive phenotypes. Our transdiagnostic analyses revealed significant differentiation of ASD and ADHD across subcortical-cortical circuits. While ASD was characterized by widespread thalamocortical hyperconnectivity and bidirectional elevated coupling across thalamic subdivisions, ADHD exhibited a focal pattern of striatocortical disruption, anchored predominantly within the caudate. Multivariate analyses identified shared and disorder-specific brain-behavior associations. Across both conditions, aberrant striatocortical signaling was associated with reduced overall intelligence measures. Clinically, ASD-related thalamocortical connectivity disruptions mapped onto generalized cognitive impairment, whereas ADHD-related subcortical alterations tracked hyperactive and inattentive symptom dimensions. Our findings differentiate ASD and ADHD through distinct patterns of functional and directional subcortical-cortical dysregulations.

papers.title: Human Hippocampal Theta-Gamma Phase-Amplitude Coupling Signals the Distance to Remembered Goals
papers.authors: Huang Z, Goumas P, Bisby JA, Rodionov R, Diehl B, McEvoy AW, Walker MC, Vivekananda U, Burgess N, Bush D.
papers.abstract: In mammals, flexible navigation is believed to rely on a cognitive map of known locations supported by the hippocampus and surrounding medial temporal lobe structures. Hippocampal place cells typically exhibit spatial firing fields within a given environment. Moreover, their firing is modulated by the movement-related theta rhythm such that ‘theta sweeps’ of place cell activity encode the trajectory towards a hidden reward location during goal-directed navigation. Here, we attempted to detect signatures of theta sweeps in the human hippocampal local field potential (LFP) recorded with intracranial EEG. Specifically, we hypothesised that sequences of locations along a planned trajectory encoded by distinct cell assemblies are associated with gamma activity at successive theta phases. To test this hypothesis, we asked N=9 patients with epilepsy to perform a spatial navigation task in desktop virtual reality while we recorded LFP signals from depth electrode contacts implanted across the medial temporal lobe. Consistent with our predictions, we found an increase in hippocampal theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, a decrease in gamma power, and theta phase precession of gamma activity as hidden goal locations were approached and the sequence of locations remaining to be traversed became shorter. This suggests that goal-directed hippocampal theta sweeps during navigation are reflected in LFP theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, and that these neural mechanisms of model-based planning are conserved across species.

papers.title: Beyond High-Amplitude Events: Amplitude-Resolved Spatial and Temporal ICA Representations in fMRI
papers.authors: Vu D, Calhoun V.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Functional MRI analyses commonly reduce high-dimensional brain activity using predefined spatial summaries, such as region-of-interest (ROI) averages, or temporally selective representations, such as co-activation patterns (CAPs) and high-amplitude events. These approaches provide useful summaries but do not explicitly characterize information distribution across the continuous magnitude of spatial and temporal network expression. We introduce an amplitude-resolved framework for systematically interrogating this continuum using independent component analysis (ICA). Resting-state fMRI data in the FBIRN dataset were decomposed using spatially-constrained ICA with NeuroMark. For the temporal representation, time points were stratified according to global ICA amplitude and frequency bands, with functional network connectivity (FNC) estimated for each amplitude range. For the spatial representation, we introduce an approach that stratifies voxels according to ICA loading magnitude and generates amplitude-specific spatial similarity matrices. Linear support vector machine (SVM) classification of schizophrenia (SZ) and healthy control (HC) participants was used to probe the information retained by each representation. Discriminative information varied non-monotonically across amplitude: intermediate ranges frequently matched or exceeded the highest amplitudes, while combinations of amplitude ranges further improved classification. These findings demonstrate that informative fMRI structure is distributed across the ICA expression continuum and motivate representations that complement fixed ROI summaries and high-amplitude approaches.

papers.title: Language-associated brain representations covary with disruption of selfhood under psilocybin
papers.authors: Cooper G, Stoliker D, Astl Delgado VS, Blackburne G, Novelli L, Green DW, Das R, Razi A, Skipper JI.
papers.abstract: Language helps organise experience into an idiosyncratic, temporally extended sense of self. We therefore used fMRI to investigate whether greater similarity between subjects in the activity of language-associated brain regions accompanied psilocybin-induced loss of selfhood using fMRI. Participants heard music and viewed moving clouds at baseline and after 19 mg psilocybin. At each brain location and time point, we tested whether similarity increased with each pair’s summed rank on the Ego Dissolution Inventory (EDI; N=43). We grouped independent components of these associations by time course and decoded each group’s map with Neurosynth. Elementary visual imagery (SI; N=49) and baseline activity served as comparators. Under psilocybin, one group formed a distributed, left-lateralised frontotemporal network matching the Neurosynth language map (r=.382, spatial-null p<.001, q=.003), nearly twice the largest comparator estimate (SI: r=.208, p=.004, q=.028; baseline: r≤.12). In exploratory analyses, resting-state connectivity of this network decreased with posterior visual cortex and increased with thalamic and frontal regions. Participants with higher EDI scores showed larger changes (ρ=.455, Bonferroni-adjusted p=.048; SI: ρ=.008), most strongly for items describing loss of ego or identity (ρ=.43–.51; other items, ρ=.22–.33). We propose that language-associated systems incorporate each person’s semantic and autobiographical context into experience, and that disrupting them contributes to loss of ego and identity.

papers.title: White matter differences in adults with developmental language disorder
papers.authors: Abbott N, Banel S, Cler GJ.
papers.abstract: Developmental language disorder is a highly common yet underdiagnosed neurodevelopmental disorder which impacts receptive and/or expressive language abilities and cannot be attributed to another etiology such as hearing loss or a lack of early exposure to language. There is very little research into the brain differences that characterize developmental language disorder, especially in adult populations In this study, we used diffusion MRI to determine whether adults with DLD show differences in white matter microstructure of the brain when compared to adults with typical language. Participants included 23 adults identified as meeting criteria for developmental language disorder, as well as a group of 26 adults with typical language. White matter microstructure was examined with fractional anisotropy via diffusion tensor imaging and precise biophysical models of intra-axonal signal fraction and orientation coherence via the Standard Model of diffusion imaging, using tractometry to evaluate microstructure differences along white matter tracts. Analysis showed reduced myelin integrity in DLD in the corpus callosum, but increased myelin integrity in the left superior longitudinal fasciculus. It is yet unclear whether differences exist in childhood and are retained into adulthood, are a result of different language environments during childhood, or are a result of behavioral and neural compensation.

papers.title: Humanizing AI-generated exemplars: Human-source framing facilitates group creative ideation
papers.authors: Xiaoyong S, Lu Y, Liu Y, Ge Y, Ruan Q, Jiang K, KelongLu.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated creative exemplars are increasingly used as scalable digital instructional resources in creativity education. However, it remains unclear whether labeling identical exemplars as human- or AI-generated shapes how learners engage in group creative activities. We tested this possibility in 113 dyads using an fNIRS hyperscanning group creative ideation paradigm. Dyads completed creative ideation tasks before, during, and after exemplar-stimulation. During stimulation, the human- and AI-attribution groups received identical exemplars labeled as produced by human or AI, whereas the control group received no exemplar. Human attribution increased idea uniqueness during stimulation relative to both the other phases and the AI-attribution and control groups. AI attribution temporarily increased switching among ideation pathways. Neither behavioral effect persisted after exemplar withdrawal. The two attribution groups did not differ in exemplar-category overlap or nearest-exemplar semantic distance, but human-attribution dyads rated the exemplars as more helpful. Human attribution also increased interbrain synchronization (IBS) in bilateral premotor and supplementary motor cortices during stimulation, whereas AI attribution was associated with decreased IBS in the left supramarginal gyrus and right frontopolar cortex from pre- to post-stimulation. Thus, exemplar-source attribution shapes the process and outcome of group creative ideation, revealing an important social-contextual factor in AI-supported creativity education.

papers.title: MRI-Guided High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound in Movement Disorders: Targeting Pathologic Brain Circuits With Precision Imaging, From the AJR Special Series on Critical Anatomy.
papers.authors: Asturias A, Saez-Calveras N, Yu J, Feltrin F, Jha M, Sharma V, Maldjian JA, O'Suillebhain P, Shah BR.
papers.abstract: MRI-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (MRgHIFU) has emerged as an alternative to other neuromodulatory interventions for patients with medically refractory movement disorders, including open surgery, radiosurgery, and deep brain stimulation. Microelectrode recordings permit refinement of indirect targets during open procedures for movement disorders. However, their use is not possible during incisionless procedures, including MRgHIFU. Traditional MRgHIFU using indirect targets yields limited efficacy or adverse effects from anatomic or functional variability. Furthermore, the clinical efficacy associated with indirect targeting of subcortical gray matter structures is increasingly recognized as resulting from circuitwide neuromodulation distributed along white matter pathways. Additionally, diffusion tensor imaging tractography and white matter-nulled sequences (e.g., fast gray matter acquisition T1 inversion recovery) now enable patient-specific targeting of pathologic brain circuits. These developments are prompting growing interest in MRgHIFU for direct targeting of disease-specific white matter tracts. In essential tremor, dentatorubrothalamic tract targeting by MRgHIFU has shown high tremor suppression with few adverse effects; in Parkinson disease, pallidothalamic tract targeting has likewise emerged as a promising intervention. These tract-based approaches can leverage patient-specific targeting to improve precision, efficacy, and safety. Future developments, including artificial intelligence-driven approaches, are expected to enhance MRgHIFU targeting and broaden its role in personalized movement disorder therapy.

papers.title: Severe Hypoxic-ischaemic Encephalopathy and Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Following Accidental Butane Exposure: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Tiburzi SP, Nistico' R, Stivala V, De Luca A, Justiz-Pérez I, Putignano A, Vescio V.
papers.abstract: Background Butane is a highly lipophilic aliphatic hydrocarbon widely used as a domestic fuel and aerosol propellant. Acute exposure in enclosed environments may cause severe neurological and cardiovascular toxicity through oxygen displacement, respiratory depression, myocardial sensitisation to catecholamines, and potentially direct toxic effects. Case presentation A 45-year-old woman was found unconscious in a small, closed studio apartment, while her husband was found deceased in the same environment. Subsequent inspection by the judicial authorities identified deterioration of the gas tubing associated with a gas leak. The patient presented in deep coma (Glasgow Coma Scale score 5) and required tracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation. Initial carboxyhaemoglobin was 16.9% and progressively normalised during oxygen therapy. Brain imaging demonstrated extensive cortical, deep grey matter, brainstem, cerebellar, and white-matter abnormalities consistent with severe hypoxic-ischaemic injury. Cardiac evaluation showed mild ST-segment elevation, increased cardiac biomarkers, and severe transient Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction (LVEF 25%) with a pattern highly suggestive of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy; LVEF subsequently improved to 44%. Severe neurological impairment persisted, and the patient was transferred to neurological rehabilitation. She died approximately six months after the index event; reliable documentation of the precise cause of death was unavailable. Conclusion This case illustrates the severe neurological and cardiovascular consequences that may follow accidental butane exposure in an enclosed environment. The coexistence of extensive hypoxic- ischaemic brain injury and transient stress-related ventricular dysfunction highlights the importance of integrated neurological, cardiological, and toxicological assessment.

papers.title: Mechanistic Disruption of the Blood-Brain Barrier and Neurovascular Unit by Lead, Manganese, and Cadmium: A WHO-WHY-WHAT-WHEN-WHERE-HOW Structured Review.
papers.authors: Lara-Estrada R, Molina-Gonzalez M, González-Santoyo I, Diaz-Ruiz A, Rios C, Horton M, Roldan-Valadez E.
papers.abstract: Environmental exposure to lead (Pb), manganese (Mn), and cadmium (Cd) damages the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) and the Neurovascular Unit (NVU) through a combination of pathways, including endothelial and astrocyte remodeling, transport dysregulation, oxidative and inflammatory signaling, and altered astrocyte-pericyte control of capillary tone. These changes lead to impaired neurovascular coupling and reduced cerebral blood flow. We collated and synthesized mechanistic evidence from experimental and clinical studies conducted over the 30 years from 1995 to 2025, focusing on studies that reported quantitative environmental exposure data and measured neuroimaging correlates of NVU/BBB injury. Cognitive deficits are associated with low-level blood lead levels (<5-10 μg/dL); blood manganese (Mn) levels of 4-15 μg/L are associated with neurodegeneration. Cadmium (Cd) is a cumulative neurotoxicity biomarker linked to cognitive deficits. Hair Mn tracks chronic inhalation exposure more closely than blood Mn does, and the gap between the two measures suggests that cerebral targets receive more manganese than systemic concentrations imply. Neuroimaging corroborates these mechanistic pathways, documenting region-specific cortical and subcortical volume loss, altered brain perfusion, and changes consistent with inflammatory signaling and with endothelial and astrocyte remodeling. Pallidal T1-weighted MRI and Arterial Spin-Labeling (ASL) perfusion MRI both perform well as neuroimaging biomarkers. Multimetal exposure biomarkers are more indicative of the mixture effect than single metal biomarkers. Longitudinal, mechanistic, and quantitative analyses indicate potential to develop interventions in exposed populations.

papers.title: Cellular senescence changes and their association with brain structure in schizophrenia and major depressive disorder
papers.authors: Okada N, Seitz-Holland J, Ikegame T, Omileke F, Kiyota M, Shoji E, Mori S, Morita S, Koshiyama D, Satomura Y, Koike S, JINDE S, Yagishita S, Kamiya K, Abe O, Shenton M, Kubicki M, Kasai K.
papers.abstract: Abstract Individuals with schizophrenia (SZ) and major depressive disorder (MDD) may experience accelerated biological aging, potentially linked to cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). While the SASP index has been reported to be elevated in MDD, its status in SZ and its relationship with brain structure remain unclear. This study investigated whether the SASP index, a composite biomarker-based measure, is elevated in SZ and MDD, and examined its associations with brain-predicted age difference (brain-PAD) and regional brain morphology across SZ, MDD, and healthy controls (HCs). A total of 119 subjects (29 individuals with SZ, 40 individuals with MDD, and 50 HCs) underwent both peripheral blood collection and MRI scanning. First, across all subjects, the effects of diagnostic groups on SASP indices were assessed. Second, associations between age-adjusted SASP indices and brain-PAD were examined within each diagnostic group. Third, exploratory analyses tested associations between SASP indices and subcortical volumes as well as cortical thickness and surface area in each diagnostic group. We found a significant main effect of diagnostic group on SASP indices and significantly elevated SASP indices in both SZ and MDD. Although no significant associations were observed between SASP indices and brain-PAD in any diagnostic group, negative associations were identified in SZ between SASP indices and the surface area of the left transverse temporal gyrus and the right inferior frontal gyrus pars triangularis, regions that play pivotal roles in auditory and language processing alterations observed in SZ. These findings suggest that SASP-related processes may contribute to the neural underpinnings of SZ through localized, rather than global, alterations in brain structure.

papers.title: Beyond Gray Matter: White Matter Functional Network Signatures of Major Depressive Disorder Track Symptom Severity
papers.authors: Calhoun V, Sridhar M, Baker B.
papers.abstract: Abstract Resting-state neuroimaging studies in major depressive disorder (MDD) have consistently identified abnormalities across large-scale gray matter (GM) networks, including the default mode, salience, and sensorimotor systems. Although prior work has primarily focused on GM, evidence suggests that white matter (WM) hemodynamic signals are meaningful and reliable, supporting an active role for WM in brain function. A key gap remains in understanding WM functional network connectivity (FNC) and spectral characteristics in MDD. We used resting-state fMRI scans from the MDD-DIRECT phase II study, comprising 1,944 participants across 13 sites, to examine WM FNC and spectral characteristics in individuals with MDD and healthy controls using a spatially constrained independent component analysis (ICA) framework. This hybrid framework leverages ICA’s ability to identify spatially robust, functionally meaningful brain networks guided by replicable spatial priors to examine WM (1) FNC differences and (2) spectral power alterations between MDD and healthy participants. MDD was characterized by reduced long-range integrative connectivity alongside increased localized and limbic–sensorimotor coupling within WM networks, highlighting a systems-level imbalance in neural communication that may underlie core cognitive, affective, and somatic symptoms of depression. We also observed reduced low-frequency spectral power within frontal and subcortical WM systems involved in cognitive control, emotional regulation, and decision-making.
