WM diffusion, particularly in the corpus callosum and the superior longitudinal fasciculus, mediated the associations between CM severity and both PTSD (MD bab = 0.022, AD bab = 0.019-0.034) and post-concussive symptoms (MD bab = 0.028-0.040, AD bab = 0.032-0.047). Findings suggest that WM alterations are more strongly associated with CM itself than with either PTSD and/or mTBI. Mediating effects in regions critical for sensory integration highlight the role of WM microstructure as a neurobiological pathway through which CM might predispose to post-traumatic symptoms.

papers.title: Sex differences in responses to neurosteroid therapy after preterm birth.
papers.authors: Hirst JJ, Palliser HK, Glover R, Pavy CL, Shaw JC, Moloney RA.
papers.abstract: Progesterone production by the placenta leads to elevated levels of neurosteroids in both the maternal and fetal circulations during late gestation. Allopregnanolone levels are crucial because they provide both neuroprotective and trophic support in the fetal brain. These include protecting against excessive excitation and supporting oligodendrocyte development and myelination. Pregnancy compromises and particularly premature birth reduce or totally deprive the newborn brain of this neurosteroid mediated protection and support. The premature fall in allopregnanolone levels may increase susceptibility to damage from hypoxic episodes and excitotoxicity. Reduced neurosteroid support is also associated with alterations in oligodendrocyte maturation and myelination, which may contribute to subsequent neurodevelopmental and behavioural abnormalities. This in turn contributes to the onset of behavioural disorders including attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Importantly male offspring have been shown to do more poorly after preterm birth as well as after other compromises. Increasing allopregnanolone action using the synthetic analogue, zuranolone, markedly improved myelination after premature delivery in an animal model. Treatment with the mitochondrial translocator protein (TSPO) ligand etifoxine, which promotes endogenous allopregnanolone production, provided protective effects in primary cell cultures following oxygen-glucose deprivation in vitro. Prematurely delivered male offspring showed markedly increased hyperactive behaviour which was also reversed by zuranolone therapy. Female offspring exhibited reduced myelination following preterm birth, without evidence of oligodendrocyte maturational arrest, and this hypomyelination was restored by zuranolone therapy. In contrast, males showed oligodendrocyte maturational arrest and a hyperactive behavioural phenotype. Together, these findings suggest that the effects of preterm birth on white matter development may differ between males and females. These findings support further investigation of allopregnanolone replacement therapy after preterm birth, including pharmacokinetic, safety, toxicology and efficacy studies in neonatal populations.

papers.title: Sex differences in functional connectivity in individuals with internet gaming disorder: a resting-state fMRI Study.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Xu X, Cui S, Dong GH.
papers.abstract: Objective Sex differences may help explain the heterogeneity of internet gaming disorder (IGD), but their neural basis remains unclear. This study examined sex-related alterations in functional connectivity (FC) in IGD. Methods 373 participants (85 males with IGD, 62 females with IGD, 141 male recreational game users [RGUs], and 85 female RGUs) underwent resting-state fMRI. The study used a 2 (group: IGD/RGU) × 2 (sex: male/female) between-subjects design. ReHo and FC were analyzed under this design with age as a covariate. ReHo interaction clusters served as seed ROIs for whole-brain FC analyses, followed by simple effect analyses for significant FC interactions. Results ReHo showed significant sex-by-group interactions in the bilateral postcentral gyrus, right middle cingulate cortex, and right fusiform gyrus. Seed-based FC showed significant interactions involving these regions. Simple effects indicated that, relative to same-sex RGUs, males with IGD predominantly showed lower FC, whereas females with IGD more often showed higher FC in connections involving perceptual processing, sensorimotor integration, behavioral regulation, self-related processing, and executive control. Conclusions IGD-related brain functional abnormalities may exhibit sex differences across multiple inter-regional FC patterns, providing new evidence for the sex-related heterogeneity in IGD. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings reflect associations rather than causal effects.

papers.title: Using data-driven, lesion-symptom mapping to study the relationship between neural and theoretical components of numeracy.
papers.authors: Duricy E, Durisko C, Fiez JA.
papers.abstract: Numeracy, the ability to understand and manipulate numbers, is a crucial foundational ability for many daily life skills. Numeracy tasks have been categorized using different taxonomic approaches, and understanding of the relationship between tasks categories and neural models of numeracy remains poor. In this study, we use the lesion method to address this key gap. The study employs a data-driven approach with support vector regression lesion-symptom mapping (SVR-LSM) of extracted factors from two left hemisphere chronic stroke survivor datasets: one with data from a battery of math and language tests (N = 100) and the other with data from the EC301 math battery (N = 64). We find that our data best support a separation of number tasks requiring verbal vs. magnitude number knowledge, aligning with a broad theme that emerges across theories in different variations. This is supported by distinct neuroanatomical correlates that link verbal coding of number to the language-centered regions including left perisylvian area and insula, and that link magnitude coding to the parietal lobe, as described in prior models. Our findings indicate that these two different sources of representation variously contribute to a range of math tasks, including different types of arithmetic calculation tasks, in ways which cannot be cleanly defined by one singular theoretical model of math cognition.

papers.title: Characterizing hippocampal activation during pattern separation with multi-echo fMRI in cognitively normal older adults.
papers.authors: Solar KG, Kashyap S, Deom N, Uludağ K, Zotovic L, Lanctôt K, Black SE, McAndrews MP.
papers.abstract: Hippocampal hyperactivity, detected with mnemonic similarity task (MST) fMRI, is both a promising marker of risk and a probable driver of degeneration in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, implementation of such fMRI in interventional research is limited by long scan times and the absence of a framework for identifying prospective participants with hyperactivity who could be targeted with therapeutic approaches aimed at reducing this activity. We used multi-echo fMRI during the MST, an episodic memory task previously shown to engage hippocampal subfields CA3 and dentate gyrus (DG), to characterize activity profiles in 33 cognitively normal older adults. We compared MST-related CA3 and DG activation and behavioural performance across subsets of eight task runs. Behavioural and activation effects were equivalent for the first set of four runs (Runs-A) and the second set (Runs-B), suggesting that robust data can be obtained with four runs. Left and right CA3 + DG activation did not differ. We provide an exemplar framework for the derivation of a threshold for single-participant classification of elevated hippocampal activation as an indicator of AD risk in cognitively normal older individuals. Scalable (~22 min) multi-echo MST fMRI robustly captures hippocampal activation and provides a framework for individual-level characterization of hippocampal function in cognitively normal older adults. This enables individualized detection of elevated hippocampal activation as a modifiable risk factor and may guide enrolment into prevention trials targeting preclinical AD.

papers.title: Neurophysiological Correlates of Target-Related Visual Attention Processes as a Function of Reward in Connection with Schizotypy.
papers.authors: Hübner N, Lockhofen D, Debnath R, Mulert C.
papers.abstract: In everyday life, we constantly select and perceive relevant information while suppressing irrelevant sensory input. This selection process is governed by the interaction between bottom-up and top-down attention mechanisms. Recent studies also highlighted the influence of reward on attention, with monetary rewards shown to enhance task performance and modulate stimulus salience. Schizotypy, conceptualized as a continuum ranging from healthy states to schizophrenia symptoms, provides a framework for the investigation of these mechanisms in non-clinical populations. This study investigated the behavioral and neurophysiological correlates of visual attention and reward processing, and their relationship with schizotypy traits. Thirty-six healthy participants were divided into two groups which performed a visual attention task with salient distractors and rewarded (target reward group, TR) or not rewarded (no reward group, NR) target stimuli while EEG was recorded. Additionally, schizotypy was assessed using the Schizotypal Personality Questionnaire (SPQ). The results showed that salient, but task-irrelevant distractors increased response times compared to target-only trials irrespective of reward. On the neurophysiological level, distractors decreased target prioritization in the NR group. Furthermore, participants with higher scores on the negative schizotypy dimension showed stronger target prioritization, especially in the absence of salient distractors. These findings suggest that monetary rewards can modulate attentional control mechanisms and that negative schizotypy traits are linked to altered attentional prioritization.

papers.title: EEG Microstates are Not Associated with Psychotic Symptoms, Neurocognitive Domains or Psychosocial Functioning in Adolescents and Young Adults with Clinical High Risk for Psychosis.
papers.authors: Liebrand M, Wedekind C, Katsarakis A, Diezig S, Michel C, Schultze-Lutter F, Kaess M, Hubl D, Koenig T, Kindler J.
papers.abstract: EEG microstates are brief and discrete topographic patterns of electrical brain activity. Microstates last for 60-120 milliseconds, are thought to represent transient, quasi-stable neural networks, and traditionally four distinct classes (A-D) are distinguished. One of the core concepts of present neuroscience is that neuroimaging is able to capture meaningful networks of brain activity, which can be translated into specific cognitive functions. Following this idea, each microstate might correspond to specific core brain functions. Importantly, these cognitive functions are impaired in mental disorders. Clinical high-risk (CHR) refers to a state associated with an increased risk of developing psychosis. Previous research has demonstrated consistent microstate alterations in CHR individuals (especially in class D), as well as in psychosis. However, the neurobiological and functional meaning of microstate alterations in CHR populations is still elusive. Since the CHR state is associated with reduced neurocognition (e.g., processing speed, verbal memory, executive functions) in combination with specific clinical symptoms and impairments in psychosocial functioning, relationships between resting-state microstates and these domains were examined in a large cross-sectional cohort of CHR individuals (n = 100). Contrary to our expectations, no significant correlations were found for these clinical measures. The finding suggests that while microstate parameters may differ between CHR individuals and controls, these alterations do not seem to directly reflect the neurobiology of clinical symptoms or neurocognitive and psychosocial functions. EEG microstate deviations as candidate trait biomarker therefore require further investigation and validation in longitudinal studies to establish their stability and predictive value.

papers.title: Cerebellar Network Organization in Parkinson's Disease: Functional Connectivity across Motor and Cognitive Circuits.
papers.authors: Lin CR, Magalhães TNC, Yonce SS, Rampalli I, Mahabir R, Bernard JA, and the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
papers.abstract: Background The cerebellum is increasingly recognized as a key contributor to cognitive reserve and network organization in Parkinson's disease (PD). However, the relationship of cerebello-cortical and cerebello-basal ganglia connectivity with cognitive status and nigrostriatal integrity remains incompletely understood. Methods Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data from 172 participants with PD in the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative were analyzed. Cerebello-basal ganglia and cerebello-cortical connectivity were investigated using region of interest (ROI)-to-ROI and seed-to-voxel approaches. Cerebellar connectivity was examined in relation to cognitive status, age, disease duration, motor severity, dopaminergic medication exposure, and contralateral putaminal striatal binding ratio (SBR). Results PD participants demonstrated robust positive cerebello-basal ganglia connectivity, particularly between lobule VI/vermis VI and the pallidum. Greater age was associated with widespread reductions in cerebello-basal ganglia coupling. Longer disease duration was associated with stronger connectivity within cerebellar and basal ganglia circuits, and among cognitively unimpaired participants, stronger lobule V connectivity with temporal regions. After adjustment for contralateral putaminal SBR, cognitively unimpaired participants generally demonstrated greater connectivity between left cerebellar regions and frontal networks, whereas cognitively impaired participants showed greater connectivity from posterior cerebellar and vermal regions, including regions implicated in cognitive processing, to temporal, parahippocampal, occipital, parietal, and somatosensory regions. Conclusions Cerebellar functional connectivity in PD shows region-specific differences across cognitive status rather than uniform network loss with cognitive impairment. These findings support further investigation of cerebellar functional connectivity as a candidate biomarker of cognitive resilience and network adaptation in PD. © 2026 The Author(s). Movement Disorders published by Wiley Periodicals LLC on behalf of International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

papers.title: An adaptive, variable-length test for certifying electroencephalographic spike-detection skill: A retrospective feasibility study.
papers.authors: Zhang T, Nascimento FA, Karakis I, Keldsen EW, Sun C, Jing J, Westover MB.
papers.abstract: Objective Determining whether an individual reader has sufficient electroencephalographic (EEG) spike-detection skill is challenging due to limited expert agreement. We evaluated whether modeling skill in interpretable signal-detection terms-discrimination ability separate from response tendency-could power an adaptive, variable-length test that can reliably and efficiently assess reader competence. Methods We analyzed a multirater dataset containing 20 521 EEG segments and 2574 rater sessions. Case signal was estimated from multirater labels, and each reader was modeled using signal-detection parameters: discrimination skill σ and response bias t . Among 368 calibration-eligible raters across five skill tiers, we used a stratified 50/50 train-validation split to select a certification threshold σ⋆ in training and to apply it in validation. We replayed an adaptive test on each rater's historical responses, using sequential stopping to issue pass, fail, or retest decisions. Results The training-derived threshold was σ⋆=.815 (95% bootstrap confidence interval = .663 - 1.018 , Youden J=.828 ). In validation, pass rates preserved the expected tier ordering: experts 100% ( 14/14 ), experienced 100% ( 4/4 ), novices 14% ( 1/7 ), residents 0% ( 0/11 ), and crowd raters 7% ( 11/150 ). In the 81-rater adaptive replay, clear failures stopped near 20 trials, and passing experts required a median of 95 trials. Split-half replay showed intraclass correlation coefficient 3,1=.87 for σ̂ at stopping; there were no hard pass-fail reversals among raters whose two halves both reached decisive verdicts. Significance A signal-detection framework quantified spike-identification skill in EEG readers, and adaptive testing estimated this skill reliably with fewer than 100 short EEG segments. This approach could provide a practical, scalable method for assessing EEG reading competence.

papers.title: Cerebral Hemodynamic Changes in Older Adults With Cognitive Complaints According to the Presence of Peripheral Artery Disease.
papers.authors: Noh S, Shin HE, Shim Y.
papers.abstract: Objective As a systemic expression of atherosclerosis, peripheral artery disease (PAD) has the potential to alter cerebral hemodynamics in elderly individuals presenting with cognitive concerns. However, how PAD status shapes the longitudinal trajectory of cerebral hemodynamics has not been well characterized. Methods We conducted a single-center longitudinal observational study enrolling 132 participants (21 controls, 39 mild cognitive impairment, 72 mild Alzheimer's disease). All participants underwent transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasonography, ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement, brain MRI, and cognitive assessments at baseline and follow-up (~13.45 months). PAD was defined as ABI < 0.90. Bilateral mean flow velocity (MFV), pulsatility index (PI), and resistance index (RI) of the middle cerebral artery (MCA) were tracked longitudinally across both time points. Results PAD was identified in 13 participants (9.8%). Baseline TCD parameters, vascular risk factors, white matter lesions on brain MRI, and cognitive measures were comparable between groups. At follow-up, the PAD group showed significantly higher MCA MFV after age adjustment (left p < 0.001; right p = 0.005). MFV increased in the PAD group (left +16.45 cm/s) but decreased in the non-PAD group (left -3.37 cm/s), with a significant between-group difference. PI and RI did not change in either group. Cognitive and functional outcomes were similar across groups throughout the study. Conclusion These findings identify PAD as a condition associated with progressive MCA MFV elevation in the context of preserved cognition, implying that subclinical cerebrovascular changes are detectable by TCD before overt clinical worsening. Future research involving larger cohorts and extended follow-up is required to determine whether such hemodynamic changes forecast eventual cognitive deterioration.

papers.title: Complementing Engel Classification: Postoperative Scalp EEG as an Objective Indicator in SEEG-Guided Radiofrequency Thermocoagulation-A Seizure-Onset Pattern-Based Stratified Analysis.
papers.authors: Yang YQ, Zhang R, Ma H, Yang L, Qu X, Chen Q, Zhang Y.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.abstract: Background Stereoelectroencephalography-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (SEEG-RFTC) is a minimally invasive therapy for drug-resistant focal epilepsy. However, the relationship between specific seizure-onset patterns (SOPs), particularly low-voltage fast activity (LVFA), and postoperative scalp EEG normalization remains inadequately characterized. This study investigates whether LVFA predicts RFTC efficacy and whether postoperative EEG serves as an objective complement to clinical outcome measures. Objective To evaluate LVFA-dominant SOPs as predictors of seizure freedom and scalp EEG normalization after SEEG-RFTC, and to assess their interaction with MRI findings. Methods In a retrospective cohort of 25 patients, seizure-onset patterns (SOPs) were classified as LVFA-present (n = 13) or LVFA-absent (n = 12). Outcomes included Engel classification and 6-month postoperative scalp EEG. Seizure freedom and EEG normalization rates were compared, with MRI-stratified analysis. Results The seizure-free rate was 92.3% (12/13) in the LVFA-present group versus 33.3% (4/12) in the LVFA-absent group (p = 0.004). EEG normalization was more frequent in LVFA-present patients (7/8, 87.5%) than in LVFA-absent patients (4/12, 33.3%; p = 0.028); all but one patient with EEG normalization was seizure-free, the sole exception being an LVFA-absent patient who remained Engel III. In MRI-negative patients, LVFA-present had 100% (6/6) seizure freedom versus 20.0% (1/5) without LVFA (p = 0.015). Scalp EEG normalization may serve as a relatively objective marker of complete disintegration of the epileptic network, whereas some patients with persistent EEG abnormalities may still achieve seizure freedom with the aid of antiseizure medications. Conclusion In this cohort, LVFA-present SOPs are strongly associated with favorable RFTC outcomes and may represent a prerequisite for postoperative scalp EEG normalization. Postoperative EEG is a sensitive objective endpoint that complements Engel classification. Systematic PET evaluation in larger cohorts may further refine candidate selection in MRI-negative patients.

papers.title: Microstructural heterogeneity of white-matter aging and its age-dependent coupling to cognition
papers.authors: Chin R, Hu X, Ranieri J, Kim J, Oh H.
papers.abstract: Brain white matter (WM) microstructure undergoes extensive changes with age, yet the regional and cellular heterogeneity of age-related WM alterations and their impact on cognition remain unclear. Leveraging Neurite Orientation Dispersion and Density Imaging (NODDI), an advanced microstructural modelling to capture specific WM cellular properties, we investigated age-dependent relationships between advanced microstructural markers and cognitive performance, indexed by six cognitive domains derived from principal component analysis. Using a suite of standard diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and NODDI techniques in eighty-six cognitively normal adults (Young: n=33, Older: n=53), we show that age group differences are widespread across whole brain white matter, with converging region-based and voxel-level evidence implicating commissural, association, and limbic pathways. Older adults exhibited significant and widespread reductions in global fractional anisotropy (FA) and neurite density index (NDI), concomitant with increases in mean diffusivity (MD), orientation density index (ODI), and free water fraction (FWF). Critically, age moderated WM-cognition associations in a domain- and tract-specific manner: younger adults exhibited stronger coupling between commissural and association tract microstructure and language and visual memory, whereas older adults showed greater dependence on projection and limbic tracts for executive and language function. The observed age-dependent coupling between specific microstructural metrics and cognition underscores the value of advanced diffusion models for capturing heterogeneity in brain aging, reveals age-specific biomarkers of cognitive health. These patterns align with phylogenetic and ontogenetic patterns of white matter vulnerability in callosal, long-range association, and limbic pathways, and suggest cellular specificity in white matter changes associated with cognitive decline. Significance Statement Aging affects brain white matter in complex and regionally specific ways, yet the biological bases of these changes and their relevance to cognition remain challenging to disentangle. Using multi-parameter diffusion MRI modeling, we found that age-related decline follows organized spatial patterns, with the greatest vulnerability in long-range association, callosal, and limbic pathways. These regional effects arise from distinct microstructural processes, including widespread extracellular alterations and more localized changes in neurite density and fiber organization. The strength and direction of white matter–cognition relationships differ between younger and older adults, revealing age-dependent shifts in how brain structural connections support behavior. Together, these findings identify biologically meaningful dimensions of white-matter vulnerability that may explain individual differences in cognitive aging.

papers.title: How auditory rhythm perception shapes speech production: The influence of neural synchronization and rhythmic patterns.
papers.authors: Tan C, Yan Q, Zhang Q.
papers.abstract: Auditory rhythm perception facilitates language processing, yet it remains unclear how neural synchronization to external rhythms contributes to speech production. The present study examined whether individual differences in neural synchronization modulate rhythmic priming effects during speech production and whether such effects depend on the rhythmic structure of the target utterance. Eighty-six native Mandarin speakers performed a speech production task involving two four-syllable rhythmic patterns as targets: the dominant [2+2] pattern (boundary after the second syllable) and the less common [1+3] pattern (boundary after the first syllable). Each target was preceded by a rhythmically congruent or incongruent pure-tone prime. Neural synchronization to the primes was quantified using cerebral-acoustic coherence (CACoh) between EEG activity and the temporal envelope of the auditory rhythms, and rhythmic priming was assessed using response latencies. K-means clustering of CACoh measures identified two participant groups characterized by relatively high and low levels of neural synchronization. Behavioral analyses revealed a significant Group × Target Type interaction. For the less common [1+3] pattern, low synchronizers exhibited reliable rhythmic priming, whereas high synchronizers showed little or no priming benefit. In contrast, priming effects for the dominant [2+2] pattern were modest and comparable across groups. Furthermore, higher theta-band CACoh was associated with smaller priming effects for [1+3] targets, indicating that stronger neural synchronization predicted reduced behavioral facilitation. These findings suggest that the influence of auditory rhythm on speech production depends jointly on individual neural synchronization capacity and the rhythmic structure of the planned utterance. The results provide new evidence that auditory-motor interactions in speech production are shaped by both listener-specific and utterance-specific factors.

papers.title: Brain network changes in patients with glioma-related epilepsy after frontal resection.
papers.authors: Fang S, Wang J, Zhang Z, Li Y, Sun Z, Zhou C, Wang Y, Fan X, Jiang T.
papers.abstract: Objective Clinical factors such as IDH status, preoperative seizures, and frontal tumor location influence the prognosis of postoperative glioma-related epilepsy (GRE), but the underlying network-level mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify network-based predictors of postoperative GRE. Methods The authors retrospectively analyzed 109 patients with frontal glioma (76 left sided). All patients underwent preoperative and 1-week postoperative resting-state functional MRI and diffusion tensor imaging. Changes in network characteristics, including structural-functional coupling and functional connectivity (FC), were evaluated. Using the left-sided cohort as the training set, Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was applied to identify network-based risk factors for postoperative GRE and construct a predictive model. The right-sided cohort served as a validation set. Results Patients with postoperative GRE showed reduced structural-functional coupling between the dorsal attention network (DAN) and the frontoparietal network (FPN), along with decreased FC within and between these networks. Increased DAN-FPN coupling and higher FC between the lesional-hemisphere prefrontal thalamus and the whole brain were protective against postoperative GRE. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.785 in the training cohort and 0.922 in the validation cohort (both p < 0.0001). Conclusions Altered structural-functional coupling and FC between attention-related networks are associated with postoperative GRE in frontal glioma. Enhanced DAN-FPN coupling and thalamocortical connectivity may serve as protective network markers.

papers.title: MBB-AVR: a mind-brain-body dataset with dynamic affective states in immersive virtual reality
papers.authors: Fourcade A, Ciston AB, Roellecke L, de Mooij J, Leos H, Villringer A, Carletto S, Malandrone F, Gaebler M.
papers.abstract: We present MindBrainBody-AffectiveVR (MBB-AVR), a multimodal dataset capturing continuous affective experience and both central and peripheral physiological responses during naturalistic emotional stimulation in immersive virtual reality. Forty-seven healthy adults (24 female, 22 male, 1 non-binary; age = 27.1 ± 5.4) viewed a 23-minute stereoscopic 360° video sequence, composed of computer-generated, language-free content designed to elicit high affective variability over time, presented via a head-mounted display (HTC Vive Pro Eye). While immersed, participants continuously rated their momentary valence and arousal using a previously validated rating tool with real-time visual feedback. Synchronized recordings include 64-channel EEG, ECG, respiration, photoplethysmography, galvanic skin response, and head and eye tracking with pupillometry. Participants additionally completed questionnaires including interoceptive sensibility and alexithymia. The dataset is organized following the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) and includes extracted low-level audio and video features of the stimulus. It may support research on the temporal dynamics of affect, multimodal physiological correlates of emotion, and affective computing. The dataset is available at https://gin.g-node.org/fourcade_a/mbb-avr.

papers.title: fMRI hyperscanning reveals widespread neural coupling during natural conversations
papers.authors: Mwilambwe-Tshilobo L, Tsoi L, Speer S, Zada Z, Burns SM, Falk EB, Tamir D.
papers.abstract: Conversation is one of the most powerful tools that people have for building and maintaining social connections. How does conversation bring two minds together? Here we tracked the neural dynamics between dyads during real-time conversation using fMRI hyperscanning, where both people were scanned simultaneously, to explore whether and how conversation aligns brains. Dyads engaged in natural, free-flowing conversation as they co-constructed the content of their dialogue. In a control condition, partners read aloud scripted dialogue from another dyad’s conversation, preserving the turn-taking structure while removing the co-construction. To examine neural alignment, we compared whole-brain intersubject correlation between partners in each condition, assessing both synchronous and predictive neural dynamics. Results showed that naturalistic conversation led to significant widespread neural alignment across brain regions implicated in attention, audition, affect, executive control, and social cognition, compared to scripted conversation. Temporally refined analyses showed that during naturalistic conversation, relative to scripted conversation, both speakers and listeners anticipated each other within a short temporal window, with brain activity preceding their partner’s in the same neural systems. These findings show that live, turn-taking conversations align neural activity well beyond passive or asynchronous communication, providing a foundation for future research examining how spontaneous, co-constructed dialogue allows people to communicate effectively.

papers.title: Increasing cerebellar beta rhythms shifts cerebral oscillatory signatures of context-driven language processing
papers.authors: Ambichler S, Portier T, Piai V, Klaus J.
papers.abstract: While there is growing consensus that the cerebellum is part of the cerebrally centred network underlying language processing, the direct nature of its contribution to comprehension and production remains unknown. In particular, while both processes require lexical access, production additionally involves motor processes linked to articulatory planning, which has fuelled the view that the cerebellum is primarily involved in motor control in language production. Cortically, both lexical access and articulatory planning are known to be driven by alpha-beta power decreases. To disentangle cerebellar involvement in language, this study investigated the modulatory effect of transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) over the right cerebellum on context-driven language comprehension and production. In a cross-over, double-blind, sham-controlled within-participants design, 32 healthy volunteers received 20 minutes of 20-Hz tACS (2 mA peak-to-peak) targeting the right posterior cerebellum. Immediately afterwards, they performed a context-driven language task while EEG was recorded from 32 channels. In the task, visually presented lead-in sentences creating a constraining or unconstraining context were followed by a picture depicting the final word of the sentence. Participants were instructed to name the picture (production) or judge its animacy (comprehension). Responses became slower overall following active compared to sham tACS, and this increase was more pronounced in the comprehension task. In line with previous work, reliable context-related oscillatory power decreases were observed in response to the context manipulation, but exhibited a different pattern across tasks and stimulation conditions. For production, beta-centred power decreases following sham shifted to temporally and spatially extended alpha power decreases following active tACS. By contrast, alpha-centred power decreases following sham tACS in the comprehension task increased following active tACS. Increasing beta activity in the right posterior cerebellum thus affected early stages of context-driven language processing linked to lexical access in both language domains. The stimulation-induced spectral, spatial and temporal shifts suggest recruitment of alternative cortical resources as a consequence of cerebellar network modulation. This interpretation is consistent with the cerebellum functioning as a network node coordinating temporal dynamics across distributed language regions.

papers.title: Neural Correlates of Beat Processing in Infancy and Their Association With Later Grammar Development: Evidence for the Atypical Rhythm Risk Hypothesis
papers.authors: Ladanyi E, Nayak S, Bush CT, Wang Y, Woynaroski TG, Lense MD, Leonard MK, Gordon RL.
papers.abstract: Infants show evidence of beat processing from birth, but its neural correlates in infancy remain poorly understood. Moreover, although rhythm and grammar abilities are closely linked in older (school-aged) children, it is not known whether individual differences in infant beat processing lay the foundations for those associations. This longitudinal EEG study examined neural correlates of beat processing in 6–12-month-old infants (N=37) and their relation to sentence comprehension skills in the same children at 4 years. We analyzed infants’ evoked time–frequency responses to rhythmic tone–tone–rest sequences presented in physically accented conditions and in inferred-beat conditions, in which accents were removed after an initial exposure phase.. Analyses revealed a significant increase in power to physically accented beats (9–24 Hz, p < .001). Individual differences in this response were positively associated with receptive grammar performance at age 4, assessed with the TROG-2 (r = .48, p = .005), and remained significant after controlling for infant age, parent education, and home music environment (β = .45, p = .011). The inferred beat effect was not related to later sentence comprehension performance. These findings indicate that infant neural activity tracks beat structure, with neural correlates broadly similar to those reported in adults, and that early neural sensitivity to beat is associated with later grammar development, supporting the Atypical Rhythm Risk Hypothesis.

papers.title: Effects of Spermidine Supplementation on Vascular Brain Health in Older Individuals with Subjective Cognitive Decline - An Exploratory MRI Analysis.
papers.authors: Schwarz C, Wurdack K, Hetzer S, Dell'Orco A, Wortha SM, Antonenko D, Benson GS, Horn N, Grittner U, Hofer SJ, Eisenberg T, Sigrist SJ, Schmitz D, Wirth M, Madeo F, Flöel A.
papers.abstract: Spermidine supplementation benefits brain health and function in animal models, with emerging evidence suggesting cognitive benefits in humans. However, effects on human brain health remain unclear. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (SmartAge), we investigated 12-month spermidine supplementation (0.9 mg spermidine/day) in individuals with subjective cognitive decline aged 60-90 years. This exploratory secondary MRI analysis included 75 participants and assessed changes in vascular brain health measures, including cerebral blood flow (CBF), white matter microstructure, and white matter hyperintensities. Brain volume and cortical thickness were also assessed. Regression analyses were adjusted for age, sex, and baseline measures. Between-group differences were observed in regional CBF and white matter microstructure. CBF increased in the precuneus from baseline to post-intervention in the spermidine group versus placebo (between-group difference, 4.9 ml/100 g/min; 95%CI, 1.0-8.9; η2 p=.11 [90%CI, .012-.250]; P=.015), with a similar trend in the posterior cingulate gyrus (3.7 ml/100 g/min; 95%CI, -.5-7.8; η2 p =.06 [90%CI, 0-.182]; P=.08). Fractional anisotropy in the cingulate gyrus white matter bundle remained stable with spermidine but decreased with placebo (.016; 95%CI, .002-.031; η2 p=.06 [90%CI, .004-.208]; P=.029). CBF and fractional anisotropy changes were not substantially associated. No substantial between-group differences were found in global or regional brain volume, cortical thickness, or white matter hyperintensities, and regional MRI changes were not associated with changes in memory performance, subjective cognitive complaints, or plasma soluble intercellular adhesion molecule-1 levels. This exploratory analysis identified selected regional MRI differences in cerebral perfusion and white matter microstructure among older adults at risk for cognitive decline. These findings are preliminary and require independent confirmation.

papers.title: Insights into temporal and spatial dynamics of short association fiber formation in the human fetal brain.
papers.authors: Li B, Krsnik Ž, Pierotich L, Kostović I, Warfield SK, Grant PE, Karimi D.
papers.abstract: Short association fibers (SAFs) form the local scaffold of cortical connectivity and support early functional specialization. However, their development before birth remains largely unknown. Using fetal diffusion magnetic resonance imaging from the Developing Human Connectome Project and histology from the Zagreb Collection of human brains, we present an in utero reconstruction of SAF pathways in the human brain. We tracked their volumetric and microstructural developmental trajectories in 243 fetuses spanning a critical period of connectome formation. We found that SAFs emerge before sulcal folding, initially as flat, loosely arranged pathways along the subplate-white matter interface, and later reorganize into coherent U-shaped bundles. Their maturation followed a sensorimotor-to-association gradient, paralleling cortical development. Nonlinear, bundle-specific trajectories captured multiphasic maturation, with subplate dynamics preceding increases in axonal coherence and early myelination. These findings reveal how the brain's local wiring is established during prenatal development and provide insight into the origins of individual variability.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注人胎儿大脑短联络纤维在出生前如何形成，结合胎儿弥散磁共振成像与组织学资料重建其宫内发育路径。作者追踪短联络纤维的体积与微结构轨迹，发现其在脑沟折叠前即出现，起初沿板下区与白质交界松散排列，后重组为连贯U形束，成熟顺序由感觉运动区向联合区推进。束特异性非线性轨迹显示多阶段成熟，板下区变化先于轴突连贯性提高和早期髓鞘化。这些结果揭示了产前局部连接的建立过程，并为个体差异起源提供线索。

papers.title: Altered Neurovascular Coupling in Obstructive Sleep Apnoea: Assessment via CBF-ALFF Spatial Coupling.
papers.authors: Liu H, Huang X, Gong S, Lu L, Wang Z, Li X, Liu B.
papers.abstract: Objectives To investigate alterations in CBF-ALFF spatial coupling in obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA). Methods Thirty-two patients with OSA and 32 healthy controls（HCs） matched for sex, age, and education background were recruited for this work. All participants received arterial spin labelling (ASL) and resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) examinations. Cerebral blood flow (CBF) and amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) maps were derived from ASL and fMRI data, respectively. Between-group comparisons were performed to identify differences in ALFF, CBF, and CBF-ALFF coupling metrics. Subsequently, correlation analyses were conducted in OSA patients to investigate whether CBF/ALFF ratios derived from brain regions exhibiting significant group-level differences were associated with polysomnographic and clinical parameters. Results Patients with OSA exhibited reduced global spatial CBF-ALFF coupling relative to HCs. Regionally, decreased CBF/ALFF ratios were primarily observed in the left parahippocampal gyrus, whereas increased ratios were located mainly in the default mode network (DMN), including the left precuneus, right angular gyrus, and left inferior parietal lobule. Conclusions This study demonstrated disrupted spatial CBF-ALFF coupling in OSA patients. Such coupling alterations reflect broad OSA-associated pathophysiological changes, including but not limited to neurovascular dysfunction, offering new insights into the neuropathological mechanisms of OSA. Advances in knowledge Using combined BOLD and ASL imaging, this study provides the first characterization of both global and regional CBF-ALFF coupling alterations in OSA, revealing distinct uncoupling signatures in the DMN and medial temporal lobe that deepen our understanding of OSA-related neurovascular pathophysiology.

papers.title: Comparing Maximally Collapsing Metric Learning and Optimized Tunable Q-Wavelet Transform for Schizophrenia Identification Using EEG Signals.
papers.authors: Djemili R.
papers.journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a noninvasive technique for recording brain electrical activity and supporting the assessment of psychiatric disorders. This study proposes a framework for distinguishing individuals with Schizophrenia (SZ) from healthy subjects using EEG data. The approach employs a transformer based on Maximally Collapsing Metric Learning (MCML) applied to feature-vector matrices and compares it with optimized Tunable Q-Wavelet Transform (TQWT) decomposition. Eight nonlinear features are extracted from both approaches and evaluated using *k*-Nearest Neighbor (*k*-NN), Optimized Decision Tree (ODT), and Deep Neural Network (DNN) classifiers. Results achieve accuracies of 100%, 99.94%, and 99.91%, respectively, using one electrode channel.

papers.title: White matter signatures of addiction diverge across opioids, cannabis and nicotine and predict impulsive choice in cannabis dependence.
papers.authors: Nkrumah RO, Wetzel L, Böhmer J, Eidenmueller K, Bach P, De Santis S, Walter H, Sommer WH, Ende G.
papers.abstract: White matter (WM) microstructure is implicated in the neurobiology of substance use disorders (SUDs), yet direct comparisons across substance-dependence syndromes remain scarce. It is also unclear whether WM abnormalities relate to impulsive decision-making and substance use severity. We performed a cross-sectional, dual-centre diffusion MRI study and quantified WM microstructure using diffusion tensor imaging and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging in 87 individuals with SUDs (48 with cannabis dependence (CUD), 16 with opioid dependence (OUD), and 23 with nicotine dependence (NUD)) and 53 nonsmoking healthy controls. Whole-brain tract-based spatial statistics and tract-specific analyses of the middle longitudinal fasciculus (MLF), a temporo-parietal tract implicated in cognitive control and valuation, were performed. OUD and CUD exhibited convergent, widespread WM abnormalities characterised by reduced fractional anisotropy and increased mean diffusivity and orientation dispersion across fronto-temporo-parietal and limbic pathways, including the superior longitudinal fasciculus, arcuate fasciculus, cingulum, and MLF. In contrast, NUD showed more circumscribed alterations observed primarily in MD and localised mainly to anterior and callosal white matter regions. In CUD, higher MLF orientation dispersion was associated with steeper delay discounting (r = 0.41, p = 0.011). Moderated mediation analyses indicated that this association was indirectly driven by cannabis consumption, with asignificant conditional indirect effects observed only among daily users. No significant MLF-discounting associations were observed in OUD. Our findings reveal both shared and distinct WM alterations across SUDs and identify a link between MLF microstructure and impulsive choice in cannabis dependence.

papers.title: Analysis of brain iron deposition in an in vivo model of pediatric autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.authors: Steinbach EJS, Lee CY, Magnotta VA, Lullmann O, Poirier M, Sowers LP, Xie J, Huang CL, Harshman LA.
papers.abstract: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) represents one form of chronic kidney disease (CKD) affecting the pediatric population. CKD in early life has been associated with neurocognitive deficits and disturbances in iron metabolism. Excess iron accumulation may exacerbate inflammatory and oxidative stress pathways linked to neurocognitive decline in CKD. No animal studies have yet investigated brain iron metabolism in early-life CKD, including PKD, or confirmed these findings through histological analysis. Utilizing a conditional Pkd2 knockout mouse, we investigated the effect of kidney disease on early brain development and brain iron deposition through neuroimaging and histology. By postnatal day 19, PKD mice had significantly increased blood urea nitrogen (BUN, mean = 141 mg/dL ± 0.6, p < 0.01) and cyst burden (mean = 83.1% ± 5.4, p < 0.01). Brain volumetrics did not differ longitudinally between groups; however, PKD mice had significantly shorter T2* relaxation times across multiple brain regions (total brain, gray and white matter, cerebral cortex, cerebellum, brainstem, hippocampus, and globus pallidus), indicating increased iron deposition. Perl's Prussian blue staining confirmed increased iron in the cerebral cortex of PKD mice. These findings extend prior human CKD neuroimaging data and provide a platform to investigate mechanisms of iron-mediated neuroinjury in early-life CKD.

papers.title: Mapping the psychosis spectrum - imaging neurosubtypes from multiscale functional network connectivity.
papers.authors: Ballem R, Andrés-Camazón P, Jensen KM, Bajracharya P, Díaz-Caneja CM, Bustillo JR, Turner JA, Fu Z, Tamminga CA, Clementz BA, Keshavan MS, Gershon ES, McDowell JE, Keedy SK, Ivleva EI, Hill SK, Pearlson GD, Chen J, Calhoun VD, Iraji A.
papers.abstract: Psychosis exhibits marked neurobiological heterogeneity that is not adequately captured by symptom-based diagnoses. Although prior efforts have identified subgroups, it remains unclear how latent disease variability manifests within the brain's multiscale intrinsic functional organization and whether these patterns can be leveraged to systematically identify biologically driven subtypes of psychosis. Here, we aim to identify Psychosis Imaging Neurosubtypes (PINs)-homogeneous subgroups defined solely from neurobiological features of brain function, independent of clinical or cognitive definitions, and whether these subgroups show meaningful phenotypic differentiation. Resting-state fMRI data from 2103 B-SNIP 1&2 participants were used to compute subject-specific multiscale functional network connectivity (msFNC). We then derived a low-dimensional neurobiological subspace, termed Latent Network Connectivity, which captured system-wide interconnected multiscale information across three components. Projections of probands msFNC onto this subspace revealed three PINs through unsupervised learning that spanned DSM diagnoses (Schizophrenia, Bipolar, Schizoaffective Disorder). Although defined purely from intrinsic neurobiology, PINs exhibited distinct cognitive, clinical, and connectivity profiles. PIN-1, the most cognitively impaired, showed Cerebellar-Subcortical and Visual-Sensorimotor hypoconnectivity, alongside Visual-Subcortical hyperconnectivity. Most cognitively preserved PIN-2 showed Visual-Subcortical, Subcortical-Sensorimotor, and Subcortical-Higher Cognition hypoconnectivity. PIN-3 exhibited intermediate cognition, showing Cerebellar-Subcortical hypoconnectivity alongside Cerebellar-Sensorimotor and Subcortical-Sensorimotor hyperconnectivity. Although covariate-adjusted analyses did not reveal significant clinical differences among PINs, exploratory analyses identified selective differences in YMDR, PANSS, and Age of Onset. Notably, 55% of relatives aligned with the same neurosubtype as their probands, a rate significantly higher than chance and than DSM-based alignment, suggesting potential heritability. Cognitive performance reliably aligns with distinct brain connectivity patterns, which are also evident in relatives, supporting their construct validity. Our PINs partially converged with previously reported BSNIP Biotypes with some correspondence (e.g. PIN1 with Biotype 1) but not with the other Biotypes, which were determined using integrated electrophysiological, cognitive, and oculomotor data, supporting convergent validity, while also indicating that intrinsic rsfMRI derived multiscale connectivity partitions psychosis heterogeneity somewhat differently from multimodal biomarker approaches. These findings underscore the limitations of DSM-based classifications in capturing the biological complexity of psychotic disorders and highlight the potential of imaging-based neurosubtypes to enhance our understanding of the psychosis spectrum.

papers.title: Brain functional mediation of vitamin D and development in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.authors: Tian P, Yu X, Bai M, Bian B, Liu Z, Liang Y, Zhu X, Jia F, Li D.
papers.abstract: Background Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) often present with developmental delays and brain functional abnormalities. Vitamin D is thought to play an important role in neurodevelopment and brain function, but its association with brain functional metrics in ASD remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the relationship between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] levels, brain function, and developmental outcomes in children with ASD. Methods We included 207 children with ASD and 209 typically developing (TD) children. Serum 25(OH)D levels were measured in all participants. Clinical assessments and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) were conducted in the ASD group. Regional homogeneity (ReHo) and amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF) were used to characterize rs-fMRI metrics, and mediation analyses were performed to assess whether these measures mediated the relationship between 25(OH)D levels and developmental outcomes. Results Children with ASD showed significantly lower serum 25(OH)D levels compared with TD children. Among ASD children, higher 25(OH)D levels were associated with lower Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS) scores and better performance in multiple developmental domains. Mediation analyses revealed that ReHo in the left lingual gyrus and right fusiform gyrus significantly mediated the associations between 25(OH)D levels and specific developmental outcomes. Conclusions Children with ASD exhibited reduced serum 25(OH)D levels, and serum 25(OH)D levels were significantly associated with both clinical measures and specific rs-fMRI metrics within the ASD group. Specific brain functional metrics may play mediating roles in the associations between vitamin D status and developmental outcomes, providing insights into potential neurobiological pathways related to ASD.

papers.title: Testing different metrics for syntactic and morphological complexity in aphasic discourse: A cross-genre comparison in Spanish.
papers.authors: Hidalgo Chagoya JR, Ansorena X, Jonkers R, Carrera M, Quemada Ubis JI, Mancini S.
papers.abstract: Purpose The aim of this study is to determine which of four tasks testing different discourse genres (descriptive, procedural, conversational, and narrative) is the most sensitive in detecting syntactic and morphological complexity deficits in Spanish aphasia. Additionally, we compare two approaches for measuring syntax in discourse to identify the most accurate set of metrics for discriminating group membership. Method In this comparative cross-sectional study, we analyzed the discourse of an aphasia group (N = 20) and a non-brain-damaged group (N = 14). Data was preprocessed using manual and automated procedures. We measured syntactic complexity through proxies (mean length of utterance, noun-verb ratio, and verbs per utterance), in addition to a competing 'syntactic structures' metric. The latter includes variables of subordination, left branching, relative clauses, and word integration, while morphological complexity was measured through an inflectional index. Results The descriptive and narrative tasks highlighted the most significant differences across syntactic complexity metrics between the groups. Additionally, nested binomial logistic regression models showed that the 'syntactic structures' metric predicted groups better than the proxies alone. Conclusions A comprehensive assessment of syntactic complexity can be obtained through the administration of both descriptive and narrative tasks. The measurement of 'syntactic structures' in discourse proved a fitter and finer-grained approach for group discrimination than the incorporation of syntactic proxies alone. These findings provide guidance for a precise discourse assessment in Spanish aphasia.

papers.title: Affective prosody and facial expression cues differentially augment spoken sentence and discourse comprehension for acute left and right hemisphere stroke survivors.
papers.authors: Tilton-Bolowsky VE, Durfee AZ, Bunker LD, You V, Kang J, Kim H, Hillis AE.
papers.abstract: Comprehension for spoken sentences and discourse is differentially impacted by left- (LH) and right-hemisphere (RH) brain damage, such as that caused by stroke. Comprehension deficits can have disabling effects on one's ability to process information, participate in everyday life, and create and maintain relationships. This cross-sectional, observational study evaluated differences in sentence- and discourse-level comprehension between LH and RH stroke survivors across different prosodic conditions and examined relationships between comprehension and damage to key LH and RH regions. Participants included 43 LH and 46 RH acute stroke survivors and 39 controls. All participants completed an in-house clinical assessment that included short passages presented in three conditions: neutral prosody, affective prosody, and affective prosody plus facial expression cues. Stroke survivors also completed magnetic resonance imaging. Consistent with expectations, stroke participants achieved lower comprehension accuracy than controls across conditions. LH participants' accuracy in the 'affective prosody plus facial expressions' condition was greater than in the neutral prosody condition, and total LH lesion volume was associated with performance. RH participants' accuracy in the 'affective prosody' and 'affective prosody plus facial expressions' conditions was greater than in the neutral prosody condition. Overall, both groups' scores increased linearly from Condition 1 to 3. None of the prespecified LH or RH brain regions were significantly associated with performance. Findings suggest that some acute LH and RH stroke survivors with comprehension deficits can benefit from affective prosody and facial expression cues, but different or additional cues may be needed for greatest benefit.

papers.title: Adolescent pragmatic development mirrors pragmatic individual differences in adulthood: An fMRI study.
papers.authors: Forbes Schieche C, Uddén J.
papers.abstract: Pragmatic development is still ongoing during adolescence. However, the developmental trajectory during this period is understudied and the underlying neural correlates of pragmatic development are unknown. In this study, we used an established fMRI paradigm contrasting indirect and direct speech acts in a newly acquired adolescent sample (n = 51) and a previously collected adult sample (n = 57). The adolescent sample was subdivided into Young (ages 13-15) and Mid (ages 16-18) groups and the adult sample (Old, ages 20-36) was split based on pragmatic skill level (established in separate behavioral tests). We observed age-related increases in activity in the posterior medial superior frontal gyrus, and a combination of age-related differences and adult individual differences in the dorsal aspects of the posterior cingulate cortex (dPCC). Both clusters were located outside the classic perisylvian language network. We interpret the dPCC findings in terms of its overlap with the Default Mode Network. Similar activity in the dPCC between adolescents and adults with lower pragmatic skill is consistent with a view that a delayed adolescent development may lead to persistent pragmatic difficulties in adulthood. The findings also indicate development towards context-specific processing. By studying adolescence, a presumably uniquely human extended developmental period, we provide a rare empirical angle on the question of which aspects of brain and cultural evolution contributed to the human communicative faculty.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究关注青少年语用能力发展及其神经关联，用fMRI比较间接与直接言语行为，并对比青少年与成人样本。结果显示，后内侧上额回活动随年龄增长而增强，后扣带皮层背侧则同时呈现年龄差异与成人个体差异，且两处均位于经典语言网络之外。作者据此推测，青少年语用发展与成人语用技能差异可能共享部分神经基础，发展延迟或与成人持续语用困难相关，并提示加工趋向情境特异化。

papers.title: Lateralized amyloid PET uptake and beta-band connectivity in relation to cognition in temporal lobe epilepsy.
papers.authors: Kong J, Kim HJ, So M, Lee I, Kim H, Kim YT, Kim HJ, Do S, Lim DK, Han JH, Kang SH, Pahk K, Kim JB.
papers.abstract: We examined focus-relative amyloid PET asymmetry and its associations with resting-state EEG connectivity and processing speed in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE). Thirty adults with clinically assigned MTLE (19 right-focus, 11 left-focus) underwent 18 F-florapronol PET and resting-state EEG. Regional standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) and sensor-level weighted phase lag index (wPLI) were evaluated using paired comparisons, rank correlations and exploratory bootstrap indirect-association models. Cognitive data were available for 26 participants, including Digit Symbol Coding (DSC) for 25. Under the original analytical convention, mean medial temporal SUVR was 1.066 ipsilaterally and 1.013 contralaterally (difference 0.053, 95% CI [0.013, 0.093]; p = 0.011; Cohen's dz = 0.500). The contrast differed by focus side (interaction p = 0.002) and was 0.038 under source-table reconstruction (p = 0.075). Ipsilateral SUVR correlated with inter-hemispheric beta wPLI (ρ = 0.617, q = 0.034 across 240 tests). The intra-contralateral association (ρ = 0.536) did not survive this broader correction. Indirect estimates for Trail Making Test A (0.279, 95% bootstrap CI [0.043, 0.761]) and DSC (0.151, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.114, 0.476]) did not survive correction across 136 models. Regional medial temporal PET uptake was associated with beta-band scalp connectivity in this small cohort, while focus-side heterogeneity and labeling sensitivity limit a uniform ipsilateral interpretation. Processing-speed indirect associations were exploratory and did not establish compensation or causality. Replication with structural correction, longer EEG sampling and longitudinal cognitive follow-up is required.

papers.title: Relationships between speech-in-noise comprehension, lip reading ability and cortical speech tracking in talking avatars as well as natural talking heads.
papers.authors: Riegel J, Schüller A, Jehn C, Wißmann A, Zeiler S, Kolossa D, Reichenbach T.
papers.abstract: In noisy listening environments, visual cues from a speaker's face can significantly boost speech comprehension. The underlying audiovisual integration in the brain involves tracking of audiovisual speech features in the temporal lobe. Moreover, lip reading in silence is associated with tracking of the speech envelope in the low-delta frequency band (0.5-1 Hz). Recently, digital avatars have emerged that can support speech comprehension. Yet, it remains unclear how the human brain integrates such artificial visual signals with natural speech. Here, we employed magnetoencephalography (MEG) to measure the neural responses to a natural video, an avatar generated by deep neural networks, and a degraded video serving as a control. We demonstrate that the avatar can enhance speech-in-noise comprehension to a similar degree as the degraded video, although less than the natural video. We further identify a late response at 600 ms of the neural tracking in the high delta band (1-4 Hz) that predicts audiovisual speech comprehension. In contrast, we did not find the neural tracking in the theta band to be involved in audiovisual integration. Interestingly, we further found that neural tracking in the low delta band was related to silent lip-reading performance. Moreover, the tracking in the low delta band evoked by the avatars was much weaker and occurred earlier than that elicited by the other audiovisual stimuli. Our results show that audiovisual integration can take place even later than suggested in previous work and can index speech understanding. Additionally, the low delta band and the high delta band play distinct roles in visual-only and audiovisual speech processing, suggesting potential avenues for further boosting the abilities of avatars to support speech comprehension.

papers.title: Preoperative neuropsychological prognostic factors for deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease.
papers.authors: Scarsbrook MW, Vadivelu S, Kolodisner J, Ocal J, Sargent E, Goudman L, Pilitsis JG.
papers.abstract: Background Preoperative neuropsychological evaluation is standard in deep brain stimulation (DBS) candidacy assessment for Parkinson's disease (PD), but batteries vary substantially across centers and may require 6-8 h across multiple visits. Objectives To synthesize evidence on preoperative neuropsychological prognostic factors for cognitive, functional, behavioral, speech, and quality-of-life outcomes following DBS and develop an evidence-informed assessment framework. Methods PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through May 19, 2026. Eligible studies reported an identifiable preoperative neuropsychological measure associated with DBS candidacy or selection or with a postoperative outcome assessed at least 6 months after surgery. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using QUIPS and PROBAST. Evidence certainty was evaluated using GRADE. Results Thirty-four studies comprising 3783 DBS patients were included. Among 311 extracted results, 238 involved an identifiable prognostic predictor, of which 117 (49.2%) reported adjusted multivariable estimates. Global cognition, executive function, and memory were evaluated as prognostic predictors in 21, 17, and 8 studies, respectively, with generally supportive directions when determinable. MDRS/DRS was most extensively studied but frequently directionally indeterminate, whereas MoCA, semantic/category fluency, and WCST each showed supportive directions in at least two studies. No instrument demonstrated comparative prognostic superiority. Conclusions Global cognition, executive function, and memory showed generally supportive but low-certainty prognostic associations. Based on these findings and consensus recommendations, we propose a standardized framework incorporating a clinical interview and streamlined testing battery requiring approximately 2 h to improve efficiency, consistency, and comparability across centers.

papers.title: High-definition transcranial direct current stimulation (HD-tDCS) modulates neural response for face-emotion recognition in major depression.
papers.authors: Pfeiffer P, Zavaliangos-Petropulu A, Taraku B, Schneider J, Norris V, Kozikowski SD, Woods R, Boucher M, Jog M, Narr KL.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
papers.abstract: Background Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) may alleviate depressive symptoms. Using a face-emotion recognition fMRI task, we investigated whether left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) high-definition (HD)-tDCS modulates neural circuitry associated with affective processing biases in major depressive disorder (MDD). Methods As part of an exploratory clinical trial, MDD patients were randomized to receive 12-daily 20-minute sessions of 2 mA active (n=37, age: 35.0±8.8years, 59%F) or sham (n=29, age: 33.0±10.5 years, 65%F) HD-tDCS. Clinical and task-fMRI data were collected pre- and post-treatment. Analyses compared blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) response over time between active and sham groups for processing of happy, fearful, and neutral face stimuli versus objects at the whole-brain level and within hippocampal and amygdala regions-of-interest (ROIs). Results Whole-brain analysis showed significant group-by-time interactions for fearful faces versus objects in right fronto-parietal regions (FWE, p<0.05), with the active and sham groups exhibiting increased and decreased activation, respectively. Increased right-hippocampal BOLD response for happy or fearful faces, and all faces versus objects occurred for active HD-tDCS, but not for sham (FWE, p<0.05). Left-hippocampal activity decreased for happy faces versus objects in the sham group (p<0.05). Increased right-hippocampal activity for fearful versus objects correlated with improved anxiety in the active group (p<0.05). Conclusions Left DLPFC HD-tDCS modulated distributed cortical and hippocampal circuitry involved in emotional face processing. The association between right hippocampal activation and anxiety improvement suggests a potential role for hippocampal function in treatment response and warrants further investigation as a candidate neuroimaging biomarker.

papers.title: Contribution of the medial prefrontal cortex to performance on the Traveling Salesperson Problem in rats.
papers.authors: Kazanjian L, Ehrlich A, Spaulding J, Salazar A, Tavares M, E Blaser R, Hales JB.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairments, including memory loss, disrupted spatial navigation, and poor executive function, are devastating features of many neurological conditions. Effective research into the causes and treatments of such disorders requires knowledge of the neurological mechanisms that underlie these cognitive processes. Our lab used a naturalistic spatial foraging task, known as the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP), to examine these processes in rodents. Previous studies from our lab have found that rats with hippocampal lesions or medial entorhinal cortex lesions were impaired on measures of spatial memory in the TSP task, but neither group showed impairments in measures of spatial decision-making. Given that the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) is typically involved in decision-making and receives projections from the hippocampus and medial entorhinal cortex, our lab investigated the effect of mPFC lesions on both male and female rat performance on the TSP. Our study found mild effects of mPFC lesions on TSP performance, evident as an interaction between mPFC lesions and sex, with route selection impairment correlating with mPFC lesion extent in males, but not females. These findings implicate the mPFC in spatial decision-making, particularly in male rats, highlighting the importance of considering sex as a biological variable in animal model research.

papers.title: Experiences of being diagnosed with unruptured intracranial aneurysm in a population-based health survey: A qualitative interview study.
papers.authors: Iversen MV, Rosenlund IM, Isaksen JG, Jønsson ABR, Ingebrigtsen T.
papers.abstract: Introduction Most unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIA) are small and carry a low rupture risk. Many patients are therefore not treated with occlusion but managed conservatively. Evidence on the psychological impact of living with an untreated UIA is limited and conflicting. Research question To explore experiences of receiving a diagnosis of a UIA and having to live with it over time. Material and methods The Tromsø7 health survey examined 1862 participants with magnetic resonance angiography and 85 diagnosed with conservatively managed UIAs were eligible for inclusion. We invited 24 based on purposive maximum-variation sampling according to age, sex, and aneurysm size, and 18 consented. Twelve participated in semi-structured interviews before data saturation was achieved. We excluded two because the interviews revealed exclusion criteria (cognitive impairment and treated aneurysm). Data from 10 interviews conducted median eight years after diagnosis were included in a thematic analysis. Results In retrospective narratives, many participants recalled experiencing serious worry or fear shortly after the diagnosis. Most described a subsequent process of adaption to the uncertainty through trust in clinicians, resilience, normalization and meaning-making, which enabled them to reestablish normality in everyday life. Concerns could resurface around follow-ups. Few described persistent anxiety at the time of the interview. The diagnosis motivated healthy lifestyle changes for many. Discussion and conclusion The interviews revealed substantial psychosocial impacts of having to live with untreated UIAs. We suggest these insights could inform decision-making in contexts where clinicians and patients must balance the potential benefits and burdens of imaging and surveillance.

papers.title: Altered hippocampal subfield functional connectivity and its association with back pain in axial spondyloarthritis: a multimodal neuroimaging study.
papers.authors: Xiong F, Luo Y, Liu Y, Lu F, Xue Y, Shen G, Wang Y, Wang W.
papers.abstract: To investigate hippocampal subfield volumes and resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) in patients with axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA), and to assess their clinical relevance. In this cross-sectional study, 39 patients with axSpA and 41 healthy controls (HCs) underwent 3-T structural T1-weighted and resting-state functional MRI. Hippocampal subfields were segmented using FreeSurfer, and seed-based rsFC maps were computed for 12 subfields per hemisphere. Group differences were assessed with general linear models (FDR-corrected) for volumes and permutation-based family-wise error correction with threshold-free cluster enhancement for rsFC. Partial correlations adjusted for age, sex, and education tested associations between rsFC and clinical parameters (FDR-corrected). No hippocampal subfield volume differed significantly between groups after FDR correction, although patients with axSpA showed nominally larger right CA4 and bilateral GC-ML-DG volumes. Increased rsFC between the left presubiculum and left precentral gyrus/supplementary motor area (PreCG/SMA) was observed in patients relative to HCs (permutation-based FWER-corrected p < 0.05). Presubiculum-PreCG/SMA rsFC was negatively associated with overall back pain (partial r = -0.52, p = 0.001, FDR-corrected q = 0.028), the only association surviving FDR correction across all clinical parameters. No significant associations were observed with inflammatory markers or disease activity indices. axSpA is associated with hippocampal-motor cortical connectivity, with increased presubiculum-PreCG/SMA rsFC linked to lower back pain severity, whereas hippocampal subfield volumes are largely preserved. These findings support reconceptualizing axSpA as a systemic disease with measurable central nervous system involvement and pain-related network reorganization. Clinical trials register number: ChiCTR2500111024 (October 23th 2025).

papers.title: Longitudinal spatial changes of the contralesional corticospinal tract in high-grade glioma: a within-patient DTI tractography study.
papers.authors: Li B, Liang R, Altawalbeh G, Hoenikl L, Ursu E, Schroeder A, Zhang H, Karschnia P, Negwer C, Meyer B, Wagner A.
papers.abstract: Purpose The contralesional corticospinal tract (CST) is often used as an internal reference in glioma tractography, but its longitudinal stability remains poorly understood. We explored within-patient changes in contralesional CST characteristics between primary and recurrent high-grade glioma. Methods Twenty-nine patients with paired preoperative diffusion tensor imaging at primary and recurrent assessments were retrospectively analyzed. The contralesional CST was reconstructed using anatomically guided deterministic tractography at fractional anisotropy thresholds (FATs) of 0.10 and 0.15. Tract-averaged fractional anisotropy (FA), tract length, and tract volume were compared longitudinally. Spatial changes were assessed using patient-level slice-wise centroid trajectories and paired voxel-wise analyses in standardized space, with HCP842 used as a fixed normative spatial reference. Results No longitudinal differences in FA, tract length, or tract volume remained significant after BH-FDR correction. In contrast, slice-wise analyses showed a predominantly anterior CST displacement at recurrence, with mean paired Y-axis differences of 2.576 mm at FAT 0.10 and 2.078 mm at FAT 0.15; 57 and 21 slices, respectively, remained significant after correction. Mediolateral changes were smaller and less consistent, and no voxel-wise differences survived correction. Relative to HCP842, both assessments were posterior to the reference trajectory, while the recurrent CST was less posterior. Conclusion The contralesional CST showed longitudinal spatial displacement without corresponding corrected changes in tractography-derived FA, tract length, or tract volume. These findings indicate that its spatial position may not remain fixed between primary and recurrent glioma assessments.

papers.title: Clinical and molecular spectrum of congenital disorders of glycosylation in 80 Egyptian patients.
papers.authors: Abdel-Hamid MS, Abdel-Ghafar SF, Issa MY, ElNaggar W, Elbendary HM, Rafat K, Gaboon N, Noureldeen MM, Rezk ZN, Elkhateeb N, Selim L, Gleeson JG, Zaki MS.
papers.abstract: Congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG) represent a diverse group of inborn errors of metabolism caused by defective glycosylation processes, usually characterized by multiorgan involvement and overlapping clinical symptoms. This study aimed to decipher the clinical and genetic landscape of CDG in Egypt to enumerate the most common CDG types and unveil potentially new candidate genes. The study included 80 patients from 57 families with molecular findings consistent with CDG. Consanguinity was noted in 90% of the families. The most common clinical features were global developmental delay (98%), dysmorphic facies (86%), hypotonia (85%), movement disorders (48%), and seizures (42%). Vision impairment, hepatic, skeletal, and hematological abnormalities were the most frequently encountered systemic manifestations. Structural brain anomalies were commonly observed in our cohort and included thin corpus callosum, cortical atrophy, white matter abnormalities, cerebellar atrophy, and cerebellar vermis hypoplasia. Biallelic variants were identified in 94% of patients, while 6% had variants in X-linked genes. A total of 53 variants were identified in 29 genes, of which 38 (72%) were novel. The most frequent variants were in SRD5A3 (16%), PMM2 (11%), ALG1 (10%), NGLY1 (7.5%), MGAT2 (6%), and ALG11 (5%). We identified two sibs with a homozygous missense variant in CAMLG, which has been recently described in only one case, supporting its role as a new CDG type. Additionally, we described a case with the recently reported UGGT1-CDG and proposed ALG10 as a potentially new CDG gene. Our study highlights the striking phenotypic and genotypic variability associated with CDG and broadens the spectrum of variants and causative genes.

papers.title: Greater temporo-occipital gray matter volume and frontoparietal cortical thickness in post-menopausal women: a UK Biobank study.
papers.authors: Tyrovolas S, Portella MJ, Usall J, Cambra-Martí MR, Callén A, Haro JM, Núñez C, Stephan-Otto C.
papers.abstract: Menopause is a critical transitional stage in women's lives, yet evidence on its impact on brain structure remains inconsistent, and large-sample neuroimaging studies are limited. Here, we applied whole-brain morphometry techniques to evaluate differences between pre- and post-menopausal women in terms of gray matter volume, cortical thickness and cortical gyrification. We processed and analyzed T1-weighted brain scans of 4098 women (1033 pre-menopausal; 3065 post-menopausal) from the UK Biobank. Post-menopausal women exhibited greater gray matter volume than pre-menopausal women primarily in the right temporal lobe, encompassing the amygdala and the hippocampus, and extending to the left temporal lobe and occipital regions. Post-menopausal women also exhibited greater cortical thickness in the frontal lobe and the supramarginal gyrus, whereas no differences in cortical gyrification were observed. These findings were consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses addressing age differences, peri-menopausal status, and other potential confounds. The spatial pattern of differences between post-menopausal and pre-menopausal women considerably overlaps with regions affected early in Alzheimer's disease, such as the medial temporal lobe and the supramarginal gyrus. Our findings of larger gray matter volume and greater cortical thickness in post-menopausal women may reflect compensatory mechanisms. Speculatively, these findings align with the biphasic model of brain structural changes in Alzheimer's disease. Further research with longitudinal designs is required to elucidate the exact mechanisms underlying the brain structural differences associated with menopause.

papers.title: Positive association between emotional intelligence and white matter integrity in the cingulum and superior longitudinal fasciculus in healthy Japanese adults.
papers.authors: Kokubun K, Nemoto K, Yamakawa Y.
papers.abstract: With the growing intensity of global competition, understanding employees' psychological awareness has become a vital aspect of organizational management. Among related constructs, emotional intelligence (EI) has drawn considerable interest, leading to a growing body of research linking EI to specific brain structures. Nevertheless, the association between EI and fractional anisotropy (FA), an index of white matter integrity, has not been thoroughly investigated. In this study, we examined the relationship between self-reported trait EI and FA using diffusion tensor imaging data from 292 healthy adults in Japan.
